groups.title: Creatures with Might
groups.intro: Might, powers and the format of supernatural creatures.

entries.title: Magic Resistance and Penetration of Creatures
entries.summary: Creatures with a Might Score derive Magic Resistance and Penetration from it, and characters with non-Hermetic supernatural abilities have their own Penetration formula.
quotes: CREATURE MAGIC RESISTANCE: Might Score + Aura Modifier
CREATURE PENETRATION: Might Score – (5 x Might Points spent on power) + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier
CHARACTER PENETRATION: Effect Roll – Ease Factor + Penetration Bonus + Aura Modifier

entries.title: Creature Might
entries.summary: Might Score gives a supernatural creature Magic Resistance, fuels its powers through the Might Pool and sets Penetration; the Pool normally refreshes over a day.
quotes: A creature that hasn't used any powers recently has a Might Pool equal to its Might Score.
Might Pools almost always refresh to the creature's Might Score over the course of a day.
CREATURE MAGIC RESISTANCE: Might Score + Aura Modifier

entries.title: Creature Powers
entries.summary: Creature powers have no levels and instead cost Might points, with a standard format, a Penetration formula based on Might and cost, and a dispelling level equal to Might.
quotes: Power Name, X points, Init Y, Form: Description.
CREATURE POWER PENETRATION: Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost of the power) + Penetration Bonus
CREATURE POWER LEVEL FOR DISPELLING: Creature's Might Score

entries.title: Creature Format
entries.summary: Line-by-line explanation of a creature's stat block (Might, Characteristics with Cunning, Size, Confidence, Fatigue and Wound Penalty notation, Abilities, Powers, Vis).
quotes: Size 0 is the same size (volume, and thus normally roughly mass) as an adult human being.
An increase or decrease of three points of Size is approximately equivalent to a factor of ten change in size.

entries.title: Creating Creatures
entries.summary: Advice for storyguides designing creatures: start from a concept and role, then choose Might, combat statistics and power costs to suit the intended challenge.
quotes: A Might Score of 20 indicates that starting magi will have a lot of trouble affecting the creature with magic.

groups.title: Mundane beasts
groups.intro: Animals and how to build them.

entries.title: Beasts in Combat
entries.summary: Beasts can use most human combat options, usually fight as untrained groups, and may use only one natural weapon per round, the best listed first.
quotes: Regardless of how many weapons a beast has, it may only attack with one weapon in a given round.

entries.title: Creating Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Introduces the step-by-step method for building statistics for any mundane beast, for example a shapechanger's animal form.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 1: Type and Size
entries.summary: Beasts are sorted into four categories (Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts), which drive later steps.
quotes: There are four categories of beasts: Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts and Clawed Beasts.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 2: Characteristics
entries.summary: Beasts use Cunning instead of Intelligence, spend characteristic points only on the four physical Characteristics, then adjust Strength and Quickness for Size; mental Characteristics come from the beast's type.
quotes: Unlike human characters, animals only spend points on their four physical characteristics (Stamina, Strength, Dexterity and Quickness).
Add twice the Size to Strength
Subtract Size from Quickness

entries.title: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
entries.summary: Table of Cunning, Perception, Presence and Communication for each beast type.

versions.title: Mental Characteristics of Creatures
versions.summary: Table of Cunning, Perception, Presence and Communication by beast type, and how Increased Characteristics applies to beasts.

entries.title: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
entries.summary: Table of typical Size and physical Characteristics for common kinds of animal, as starting points for new beasts.

versions.title: Example Physical Characteristics of Creatures
versions.summary: Table of sample physical Characteristics for common creature types, with the rule for applying Size adjustments after spending points.
quotes: add twice the Size to Strength and subtract the Size from Quickness

entries.title: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
entries.summary: How to scale a creature larger or smaller than average, such as after a Muto Animal spell, by adjusting Strength, Quickness and wound ranges per Size point.
quotes: for every point of Size removed, subtract two from Strength (and therefore Damage total), add one to Quickness (and therefore Initiative and Defense totals), and decrease the damage range for each wound level by 1 (minimum of 1)

versions.title: Creatures of Non-Standard Size
versions.summary: How to adjust Strength, Quickness and wound ranges for creatures bigger or smaller than their type's norm, including the effect of Muto Animal size spells.
quotes: for every point of Size removed, subtract two from Strength (and therefore Damage Total), add one to Quickness (and therefore Initiative and Defense Totals)

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 3: Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Species Virtues and Flaws come free to all members of a species and are not balanced for game purposes, while exceptional individuals need balanced individual Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: It is recommended that a species have at least one point of Flaws for every three points of Virtues.

entries.title: Suitable Virtues and Flaws for Beasts
entries.summary: Lists Virtues and Flaws appropriate to beasts and a note that Improved Characteristics grants more characteristic points to larger creatures.
quotes: A creature of Size +1 or smaller gets 3 characteristic points from this Virtue as normal, a creature of Size +2 gets 6 characteristic points, a creature of size +3 gets 9 characteristic points, and so on.

alsoIn.title: Suitable Virtues and Flaws for Beasts

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 4: Basic Abilities
entries.summary: Table of the Abilities every creature of each type has, plus rules that animals with Cunning cannot gain experience or learn new Abilities as adults except through an Animal Handling teacher.
quotes: Animals (at least, those with Cunning rather than Intelligence) cannot acquire experience points to improve their Abilities once they have reached adulthood, nor can they learn new Abilities.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 5: Qualities
entries.summary: Catalog of creature Qualities (such as Ambush Predator, Constriction, Grapple, Overrun, Swallow Whole, Tough Hide and Venomous) that adjust characteristics, Abilities, Protection and special attacks, with how extra Fatigue levels are granted.
quotes: One extra Fatigue level grants an additional Winded level, two extra grant another Winded Level and another Weary Level, etc.

entries.title: Beast Creation Step 6: Combat Statistics
entries.summary: A beast's combat totals are calculated as normal using the Natural Weapons Table.
quotes: Combat Statistics are calculated as normal (page 393), using the Natural Weapons Table.

entries.title: Natural Weapons Table
entries.summary: Table of Initiative, Attack, Defense and Damage modifiers for natural weapons such as teeth, claws, horns and hooves.
quotes: All natural weapons use the Brawl Ability.

entries.title: Aging of Animals
entries.summary: Adjusts the age at which aging starts, the age modifier and the number of aging rolls per year for an animal from its average lifespan relative to a human's.
quotes: Thus a creature with an average lifespan of 10 years has a modifier of (50/10) or five.

entries.title: Statistics of Shapechangers
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Introduces the seven-step procedure for combining a human's and an animal species' statistics into those of a shapechanger's animal form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 1: Characteristics
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: For each Characteristic other than Intelligence/Cunning, take the lower value if both are negative, the higher if both are positive, and otherwise add the two.
quotes: If the human and the animal Characteristic are both negative, use the lower of the two.
If the human and the animal Characteristic are both positive, use the higher of the two.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 2: Cunning Versus Intelligence
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Shapechangers normally keep human Intelligence, though lycanthropes lose it for Cunning; a worked example combines a magus's and a wolf's Characteristics.
quotes: In most cases, the shapechanger retains human Intelligence.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 3: Size
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: The animal form uses the animal's Size; a Size-affecting Virtue or Flaw makes the character a notably large or small member of the species.
quotes: Human Size has no impact on the Size statistic of the shapechanged form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 4: Virtues and Flaws
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Virtues and Flaws of both human and animal forms apply in animal form, but a duplicate applies only once.
quotes: If the animal form already has a Virtue or Flaw possessed by the character, it applies only once.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 5: General Abilities
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: A shapechanged character uses the animal form's General Abilities, keeping only languages, lores, Supernatural Abilities and (if Intelligence is retained) Arcane and Academic Abilities.
quotes: Use the General Abilities of the animal form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 6: Communicating
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: A shapechanger can communicate with animals of the same or similar species, grouped by temperament, aspect, diet and habitat.
quotes: Acquire the ability to communicate with members of the same or similar species as the shapechanged form.

entries.title: Shapechanger Step 7: Wounds and Experience
entries.requires: Shapechanger (for example House Bjornaer Heartbeast or Skinchanger)
entries.summary: Wounds carry between human and animal forms (lycanthropes heal animal-form wounds on reverting), and experience gained in animal form may go to animal-form Abilities.
quotes: Any wounds taken in the human form are reflected in the animal form, and vice versa.

entries.title: Beasts as Characters
entries.requires: Playing a beast or enchanted animal as a character
entries.summary: Explains how beast characters are built: each species has unbalanced species Virtues and Flaws, exceptional beasts may add balanced individual ones, and normal beasts can improve existing Abilities but only learn new ones if trained, while intelligent beasts advance normally.
quotes: Normal Beasts cannot learn new Abilities unless Trained, but can improve existing Abilities; intelligent beasts can improve as normal.

entries.title: Animal Grogs
entries.summary: Introduces animals as grog characters, with guidance on which Sizes and kinds of animal make the best player characters.
quotes: creatures between the Sizes of –3 and +2

entries.title: Animal Physical Form
entries.summary: Explains what an animal body prevents (grasping and using tools) and grants (natural protection, natural weapons and abilities like flight or swimming), and that listed Quality modifiers are not applied.
quotes: which grant an intrinsic Protection of at least 1

entries.title: Animal Cunning Instead of Intelligence
entries.summary: Animals have Cunning rather than Intelligence, act by instinct and Personality Traits, cannot reason logically, and must take the Restricted Learning Flaw.
quotes: The Cunning characteristic possessed by beasts means that they act largely through estimation (also called instinct), and are ruled by their Personality Traits.

entries.title: Animal Language Abilities
entries.summary: Animals cannot speak, have no automatic Native Language, learn human languages slowly depending on Cunning, and have a species Language Ability that cannot be raised with experience.
quotes: an animal always has a Source Quality of (4 + Cunning)

entries.title: Animal Aging Table
entries.summary: A table giving lifespan, starting age, the age aging begins, the modifier to aging rolls and the number of aging rolls per year for humans and several kinds of animal.
quotes: | Hoofed Beasts | 27 | 3 | 20 | +1 per 5 years | 2 per year |

entries.title: Animal Aging Rate
entries.summary: Shows how to scale the human aging figures to any creature's average lifespan, covering the age aging begins, the aging-roll modifier and the number of aging rolls per year, spread across the seasons.
quotes: Thus, a creature with an average lifespan of 10 years has a modifier of (50/10), or 5.

entries.title: Animal Grog Characteristics and Size
entries.summary: Gives how Size, the Large Virtue and Small Frame Flaw affect an animal grog, the penalties to Presence and Communication when dealing with humans by animal type, and how Size adjusts Strength and Quickness.
quotes: After Characteristic points have been decided, add twice the character's Size to her Strength, and subtract the character's Size from her Quickness.

entries.title: Animal Grog Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Lists the intrinsic Flaws every animal grog has without gaining points, the required Restricted Learning Flaw, suitable Social Status options, and how Animal Ken substitutes for a Language Ability.
quotes: Animal grogs suffer from the effects of the No Hands and Mute Flaws

entries.title: Animal Grog Abilities and Experience
entries.summary: Describes the starting experience animal grogs receive for their pre-adult life, their free animal Language Ability, yearly experience, early aging and typical Abilities.
quotes: An animal grog receives 120 experience points for his pre-adult life

entries.title: Hunting Dogs
entries.summary: Game statistics for the main hunting hounds, built with the animal rules from Mystery Cults but usable without that book, used by the hunting rules.
quotes: The hunting dog statistics presented here are based upon the rules in Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults, page 38, but can be used fully without that book.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.38

entries.section: Hounds, horses and pets (Lords of Men)

entries.title: The Types of Horses
entries.summary: Explains how the horse templates (destrier, courser or rouncey, palfrey or jennet, draught horse and working pony) can be individualized, then gives each template's statistics, uses, typical price and where the best animals come from.
quotes: Horse templates typical of each type are provided that the storyguide can modify to individualize horses available at market or presented as gifts.
Owning such a beast is worth at least a single experience point in Reputation: Prudhomme.
A courser usually costs around 10 to 20 pounds

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.40

entries.section: Hounds, horses and pets (Lords of Men)

entries.title: Some Unusual Pets
entries.summary: Introduces game statistics for a few mundane pets (magpie, monkey, squirrel) built with the animal Qualities rules from Mystery Cults. Pets may be trained by their owners and the statistics can serve as templates for Magical Animal Companions.
quotes: These animals may be trained by their owners.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.40

entries.section: Hounds, horses and pets (Lords of Men)

entries.title: Some Typical Prey Animals
entries.summary: A table of combat statistics for the small game animals a hawk typically hunts, for resolving a hawking attack.
entries.section: Hounds, horses and pets (Lords of Men)

entries.title: Appendix: Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Introduces a step-by-step system for generating statistics for heartbeasts, familiars and other mundane creatures.

entries.title: Mundane Beasts 1: Type and Size
entries.summary: Defines the four beast categories (Birds, Fish, Hoofed Beasts, Clawed Beasts) and how Size steps relate to weight, with the bird adjustment.
quotes: A 1-point difference in Size doubles the weight

entries.title: Size Examples (animals)
entries.summary: Table of example animals at each Size value from -15 to +9.

entries.title: Ferocity (beast Virtue)
entries.summary: A beast-only Minor Virtue giving confidence points that can be used only in situations that trigger the animal's natural ferocity.
quotes: take 3 confidence Points and a confidence Score of 1

entries.title: Mundane Beasts 5: Qualities
entries.summary: A list of animal Qualities (Aggressive, Camouflage, Fast Runner, Grapple, Venomous and so on) that adjust Characteristics, grant Abilities or modify combat, plus how extra Fatigue levels are handled.
quotes: One extra Fatigue level grants an additional Winded level
Add +3 to all rolls involving running.

entries.title: Animal Creation Example: Bear
entries.summary: Worked example of the mundane beast design procedure, building a bear step by step and ending with a full stat block.

entries.title: Beast Statistics
entries.summary: Rules for mundane beast statistics: Characteristics outside the human range need no Virtue, Cunning replaces Intelligence, beasts cannot learn new Abilities without training, and they have no Might or vis.
quotes: Beasts do not need a Virtue or Flaw to have Characteristics outside the normal human range of –3 to +3.
entries.section: Realms of Power: The Magic Realm

entries.title: Modifying Beast Sizes
entries.summary: How to change a beast's Size by adjusting Strength and Quickness per point of Size, then updating combat statistics.
quotes: add 2 points of Strength and subtract one point of Quickness for each point of Size added
entries.section: Realms of Power: The Magic Realm

entries.title: New Virtues for Beasts (Ferocity)
entries.summary: Beasts with Ferocity get a pool of Confidence points usable only when their natural ferocity is triggered, such as defending a den or fighting a natural enemy.
quotes: take three points for you to use when those circumstances are met
entries.section: Realms of Power: The Magic Realm

gated.title: Magic characters and creatures
gated.intro: Magic creatures, magic humans, Qualities and Inferiorities.

entries.title: True Names and Synthemata
entries.requires: Knowledge of a being's True Name or synthemata (theurgy)
entries.summary: Explains True Names, which act as indefinite-duration Arcane Connections to spirits and are learned as spell-like abilities with experience points, and synthemata, the signs and passwords that every being with Might has and that theurgic magic uses to command it.
quotes: Each True Name is a spelllike ability recorded as "True Name of (Being)" on the character sheet, and costs 5 experience points to learn.
Knowing the True Name of a creature adds 5 to all lab totals to research synthemata for that same being.
A True Name is an Arcane Connection of indefinite duration

alsoIn.title: Arcane Connections, True Names, and Synthemata (Spirits)

entries.title: Animating Corpses with Magic
entries.summary: How a corpse animated by a Rego Corpus spell, demonic possession or a Magic spirit is statted: no fatigue, no powers of its own, and a Might score only when a spirit's power animates it.
quotes: Its Brawl skill is nominally 3, though as an optional rule the troupe may wish to assign a Brawl score equal to the caster's Finesse.
Regardless of how the corpse is animated, its unarmed attacks can be blocked by Magic Resistance.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.75

entries.title: Jinn (Free Virtue)
entries.requires: Virtue: Jinn (spirits of the Islamic lands)
entries.summary: Explains that Jinn is a Free Virtue marking spirits associated with the Islamic lands, who may belong to the Magic, Faerie or Infernal realm and are vulnerable to Sahir magic.
quotes: The Free Virtue Jinn marks out a category of spirits associated with the Islamic lands.

related.text: The Cradle and the Crescent, Chapters 3 and 4

entries.title: Essential Traits
entries.requires: Creatures of the Magic Realm with essential traits
entries.summary: Describes essential traits, features of a Magic Realm creature's very nature (marked with an asterisk in its stats) that magic cannot force it to act against.
quotes: Magic cannot, therefore, make them act against those traits.
They are indicated with an asterisk in the character statistics

versions.title: Essential Traits
versions.summary: Personality Traits of magic characters become fixed Essential Traits that protect against effects forcing contrary behaviour, and Characteristic-specialty traits combine with Characteristics by a set method.
quotes: if the Characteristic is positive and the Trait is beneficial, use the greater of the two; if the Characteristic is negative and the Trait is detrimental, use the lesser of the two; otherwise, add the Trait to the Characteristic

entries.title: Daimons and Aspects
entries.summary: Rules for Daimons, named spirits that stay in the Magic Realm and act on Earth through expendable Aspects, each with its own Might and Might pool. Covers how Aspects are created, destroyed, summoned and bound, and how to give a Daimon statistics if the characters ever confront one.
quotes: A Daimon is a permanent resident of the Magic Realm and cannot enter the material world; instead, it creates an Aspect as its agent on Earth.
An Aspect cannot appear within several miles of another Aspect of the same Daimon
Ordinary Hermetic magic cannot summon an Aspect of a Daimon from the Magic Realm

related.text: Dies Irae, The Twilight of the Gods

entries.title: Revenants, the Walking Dead
entries.summary: Introduces revenants as restless dead whose only form is an animate material corpse driven by a spirit, and notes that their physical statistics also serve for spell-animated corpses, which have no Might.
quotes: Such automatons are not supernatural beings and have no Might score (and hence no Magic Resistance).

entries.title: Fighting the Walking Dead
entries.summary: How magic and weapons affect revenants: body and spirit are attacked separately, Incapacitating wounds count as Heavy, Perdo Corpus spells aimed at the living often fail, and legend-specific methods destroy the animating spirit.
quotes: they cannot be Incapacitated; treat Incapacitating wounds as Heavy wounds instead.
Learning the method for destroying a revenant may require a story, or if the storyguide prefers she can assign it an Ease Factor of 9 on an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll.

entries.title: Option: Resistance to Piercing Weapons
entries.requires: Revenant creatures; troupe adopts the option
entries.summary: An optional rule letting revenants resist piercing weapons such as spears and arrows, either with a Soak bonus or total immunity, at the storyguide's judgment of what counts as piercing.
quotes: The troupe may wish to grant revenants an additional +10 Soak bonus against such weapons, or simply rule them totally ineffective.

entries.title: Magic Characters: Might and Might Points
entries.summary: Overview of what Magic Might gives a magic character: Magic Resistance equal to Might, Might Points spent on powers and recovered over time, destruction when Might is reduced, freedom from deprivation (with penalties if it is ignored), and the ability to consume vis to restore Might Points.
quotes: Magic Might gives the character innate Magic Resistance equal to its Might Score
A magic character is destroyed if his Might Score is reduced to 0 or less.
Each pawn of vis from the same Form as the character’s Might Score will immediately replenish 5 Might Points, or 2 Might Points if this vis is associated with any other Art

entries.title: Magic Character Creation
entries.summary: Introduces the procedure for designing characters that begin play with Magic Might, such as familiars, ghostly warders or magical servants.

entries.title: Magic Character Creation Summary
entries.summary: Four-step summary of making a magic character: pick a concept (true form, Characteristics, Virtues and Flaws, Size), determine season and Abilities, set Magic Might and choose Qualities and Inferiorities, then add finishing touches.
quotes: Characteristics: 7 points assigned as in standard Detailed Character Creation (see ArM5 page 29), no Characteristic more than +3 or less than -3.
A spring character receives 120 experience points, a summer character receives 360, an autumn character receives 720, and a winter character receives 1200.

entries.title: Auras and Might Recovery
entries.summary: Resting in a Magic aura speeds recovery of Might Points; a subtotal from aura and Might Score gives the time to recover the whole pool, divided by Might Score for the per-point rate.
quotes: ENTIRE RECOVERY TIME: Subtotal = Aura - (Might Score / 5), then refer to chart
RECOVERY RATE: 1 Might Point per (Recovery Time / Might Score)

entries.title: Magic Character Concept
entries.summary: First step of making a magic character: choose its true form, assign base Characteristics, decide whether it is intelligent, take the Special Virtue for its type plus a Social Status Virtue or Flaw, other Virtues and Flaws, and set Size, which adjusts Strength and Quickness.
quotes: you should begin with all eight scores at 0 and assign 7 points to them
adding two times Size to Strength, and subtracting Size from Quickness

entries.title: Magic Animal Characters
entries.summary: Rules for building a magic animal character from a mundane animal's stats: innate No Hands and Mute equivalents, required minimum Abilities, and a Size adjustment to Magic Might.
quotes: you must subtract the character's Size from its Might Score, or add to it if Size is negative

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Character Guides
entries.summary: A shorthand for storyguides: a character guide lists only the required Might, Characteristics, Virtues and Flaws, Personality Traits, Abilities and Powers for a type of magic character instead of a full sheet.
quotes: The character cannot spend experience points on any other aspect of the character until all of its scores have reached these levels.

entries.title: Magic Human Characters
entries.summary: Magic humans are designed like ordinary human characters but always look monstrous, suffering a social penalty with mundane humans and animals; magi are better designed normally and given a transformation Virtue later.
quotes: giving them a –6 to all social interactions with mundane humans or animals

entries.title: Magic Thing Characters
entries.summary: Magic things draw their Might from Size according to a minimum-Size table, can grow in Might by joining a larger entity, move slowly, are not blocked by Magic Resistance unless using an active supernatural effect, and always have Temporary Might.
quotes: The following chart shows the minimum Size required for each level of Might Score.
Magic things always have Temporary Might
All magic thing characters receive the No Fatigue Quality at no cost.

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition p.64 Hermetic Empowerment
The Mysteries Revised Edition p.66 Spirit Familiar
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.134 Bind Magical Creatures

entries.title: Cunning Characters
entries.summary: Notes on the limits of playing an unintelligent character, and the option to convert Cunning to Intelligence when the Magic realm significantly changes it.
quotes: They cannot use Confidence Points unless they have the Ferocity Virtue.

entries.title: Magic Spirit Characters
entries.summary: Magic spirits are designed from a physical form's Characteristics but are insubstantial, can be affected only by beings of the same form, are immortal unless their true form is destroyed, and always have an innate Magical Air.
quotes: Magic spirits always have an innate Magical Air that is very difficult for them to overcome.

entries.title: Magic Character Season
entries.summary: Season replaces age for magic characters and determines starting experience points: spring, summer, autumn or winter stages of development, with Abilities bought according to Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: Season is a new statistic that replaces age for magic characters
| Winter | 1200 |

entries.title: Magic Might (character creation)
entries.summary: Choose a Magic Might Score and Form from a table by saga power level and role (grog, companion, magus); the Might Score also gives an equal number of points for Magic Qualities, and is subtracted from all Advancement Totals.
quotes: You must subtract the character's Might Score from all Advancement Totals
Minor Qualities cost 1 point, and Major Qualities cost 3 points.

entries.title: Magic Character Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Final steps: at least three Personality Traits, Reputations, starting Confidence for eligible characters, an Essential Trait for its true form, combat scores, equipment and inherent vis.
quotes: (this is typically equal to its Might Score divided by 5, rounded up)

entries.title: Magic Powers
entries.summary: How Magic Qualities give powers designed like Hermetic effects, with a table of spell levels, effect types, Might costs and Initiative for each Quality, plus rules for constant powers, Penetration, Incapacitating wounds and a zero Might pool.
quotes: Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost) + Penetration bonus
Like Ritual spells, Ritual Powers are always at least Level 20, and all powers with effects of Level 50 or more must be designed as Ritual Powers.

related.text: ArM5 p.191 Penetration for Magic Powers

entries.title: Qualities and Inferiorities
entries.summary: Magic Qualities and Inferiorities are the Virtue and Flaw equivalents for characters with a Might Score; they are bought with points equal to Might, need not balance, and grogs may not take Major ones.
quotes: A character starts with a set number of Quality points equal to its Might Score

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages pp.104-109 Heroic Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Major Magic Qualities
entries.summary: List of Major Magic Qualities a magic character can buy, including Fatigue Mastery, Focus, Greater and Ritual Powers (with their Might costs and Initiative), Gentle Air, Gifted, Gigantic with its Size table, Improved Characteristic, Natural Appearance, No Fatigue and Vis Mastery.
quotes: The power has a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)
Initiative for the power is equal to the character's Quickness – (the magnitude of the effect x 2)

entries.title: Minor Magic Qualities
entries.summary: List of Minor Magic Qualities, such as Form Resistance, Gift of Speech, the Improved Abilities, Attack, Damage, Defense, Fatigue, Initiative, Might, Powers, Recovery and Soak options, Lesser Power, Minor Virtue and Personal Power.
quotes: Personal Powers have a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)
Improved Abilities: You gain 50 experience points, which may be spent on any Abilities or Arts that the character can learn.

entries.title: Major Magic Inferiorities
entries.summary: List of Major Magic Inferiorities, such as Acclimation Prone, Major Flaw, Miniature with its Size table, Monstrous Appearance, Reduced Characteristic and Temporary Might, which ties wounds to Might Points and vis.
quotes: When the character is injured, it loses Might Points equal to the penalty of the wound

entries.title: Minor Magic Inferiorities
entries.summary: List of Minor Magic Inferiorities, such as Limited Gestures, Movement and Speech, Minor Flaw, the Reduced Abilities, Attack, Defense, Fatigue, Initiative, Might, Power and Soak options, and Susceptible to Deprivation.
quotes: Reduced Abilities: Subtract 50 experience points from the character's existing Abilities

entries.title: Animal Handling (magical beings)
entries.summary: Extends the Animal Handling Ability to managing and training elementals, animate trees, animal spirits and other beings with Cunning instead of Intelligence.
quotes: you can apply the same principles when interacting with other beings that have Cunning instead of Intelligence

entries.title: Social Abilities and Magical Beings
entries.summary: Summarizes which social Abilities apply to magical beings: most work with any intelligent being, Folk Ken only covers humans and human-like beings, and Magic Lore substitutes for it when judging magical beings' motives.
quotes: Magic Lore: This may be used like Folk Ken when attempting to understand the motivations and personality of magical beings.

entries.title: Environmental Temperatures
entries.requires: Flaw: Warped Senses (Sensitive to Cold / Sensitive to Heat)
entries.summary: Chart ranking environmental conditions from unnaturally hot to unnaturally cold, used to judge how far a character with temperature sensitivity is from the conditions it is accustomed to.
quotes: Comfortable for a normal inhabitant of the Normandy, Rhine, Stonehenge, and Hibernia Tribunals

entries.title: (Form) Resistance (Ability)
entries.summary: A Supernatural Ability for characters with Magic Might that adds its score to resistance against damage from things of one Form and raises Magic Resistance against spells of that Form, but does not stack with the Parma Magica.
quotes: You may add the character's score in this Ability as a bonus to attempts to resist damage from things of that Form

entries.title: Magical Meditation (Ability)
entries.summary: A Supernatural Ability for characters with Magic Might that lets them recover Might Points faster in a Magic aura while concentrating, and prevent Acclimation at an increased rate.
quotes: it recovers 1 Might Point for each level of the Magic aura over the course of about ten minutes

entries.title: Magic Character Advancement
entries.summary: Magic characters can gain and spend experience points like other characters, but their Might Score is subtracted from the Advancement Total; consuming vis reduces that penalty.
quotes: the character's Might Score is always subtracted from its Advancement Total
If the character consumes a pawn of magic vis of any type, he may reduce the penalty to his Advancement Total by two

entries.title: Magic Qualities and Initiation Scripts
entries.summary: Describes how a rare book could teach a magic being new Magic Qualities, treated like an Initiation Script adapted by a Mystagogue.

entries.title: Transformation: spending experience on Qualities
entries.summary: Experience points can be spent to gain, swap or upgrade Magic Qualities and Inferiorities according to a cost table, or vis can be consumed as a transformational study source.
quotes: Practicing a Quality that you already possess with the intention of improving upon it has a Study Total of 5
The character must use a number of pawns of vis of any type equal to its Might Score.

entries.title: Acclimation
entries.summary: Each year a magic character that stays away from Magic loses a Magic Quality or a point of Might unless it meets one of three protective conditions.
quotes: a magic character either loses a Magic Quality, or else reduces its Might Score by 1

entries.title: Acclimation: Auras
entries.summary: A table of the minimum Magic aura strength, by Might Score and time spent within it, needed to avoid Acclimation, with a rule for visiting the Magic Realm.
quotes: treat the Magic Realm as an aura of 10 and halve the character's Might Score

entries.title: Acclimation: Effects
entries.summary: A magic character avoids Acclimation by affecting, or being affected by, a non-Might character with magic for a number of seasons each year, given by a table of Might or effect level.
quotes: a magic character with Might 15 would need to constantly affect a mundane character for three seasons every year

entries.title: Acclimation: Vis
entries.summary: A magic character avoids Acclimation for a year by consuming a Might-based number of pawns of vis, and then rolls on the Vis Consumption chart.
quotes: A magic character is safe any year in which it consumes (Magic Might Score / 2) pawns of magic vis, of any type.

entries.title: Vis Consumption
entries.summary: A stress-die chart for the side effects, botches, story events and Transformation that result when a magic character consumes vis to avoid Acclimation.
quotes: roll a stress die and consult the following chart. The number of botch dice is equal to the number of pawns of vis consumed.

entries.title: Awakened Trees
entries.summary: Trees in Magic auras are awake, with wakefulness rising with aura strength, and have Cunning instead of Intelligence and no Might score.
quotes: In an aura of level 6 or higher, the trees are fully awake and can see and hear about as well as a human can.

related.text: ArM5 p.137 Stir the Slumbering Tree

entries.title: Animated Trees
entries.requires: Trees animated by spell or spirit
entries.summary: How trees become mobile through spells or spirit powers, and when an animated tree has a Might score.
quotes: temporarily gains Might equal to the activation cost of the power

entries.title: Character Guide: An Animated Tree
entries.requires: Trees animated by spell or spirit
entries.summary: Stock statistics block to use for any animated tree, with guidance on uprooting and moving it via Manifestation.
quotes: Under most circumstances, an animate tree has no Might score.

related.text: ArM5 p.139 Lord of the Trees

entries.title: Option: Brawl Skill for Animated Trees
entries.requires: Trees animated by spell or spirit
entries.summary: Optional rule giving each animated tree its own Brawl skill, set by the caster's Finesse or by the animating spirit.
quotes: a tree animated by a spell has a Brawl skill equal to the caster's Finesse

entries.title: Trees of Virtue
entries.summary: Trees of Virtue hold 1 to 3 pawns of vis tied to their powers and can be Enriched using only part of the tree, which depletes the tree's magic.
quotes: Enriching this item, or collecting the tree's vis, depletes the tree's magical powers.

gated.title: Magic animals
gated.intro: Beasts of Virtue, dragons, magical cats and other magic animals.

entries.title: Beasts of Virtue
entries.summary: Introduces Beasts of Virtue, rare epitomes of their species that make good familiars, and notes the vis contained in their corpses.
quotes: The corpse of a Beast of Virtue typically contains 1 pawn of vis for each 5 points (or fraction) of Might it possessed

entries.title: Designing Beasts of Virtue
entries.summary: Beasts of Virtue use the Chapter 4 magical character rules with set Inherited Virtues and Flaws and no physical-defect Flaws.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Magic Animal; Essential Virtue (Major or Minor)

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Concept
entries.summary: Rules for Characteristics, the required Magic Animal and Essential Virtues, and permitted Virtues and Flaws when creating a Beast of Virtue.
quotes: You have 7 points to spend on Characteristics, just as other characters.

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Season and Abilities
entries.summary: How a Beast of Virtue's season of life sets its age and how its experience points must be spent on species Abilities.

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Guidance on spending Might on Magical Qualities, with powers restricted to those that express the species' perfection.
quotes: determine its Might and spend these points on Magical Qualities, taking Magical Inferiorities if you want more points to spend

entries.title: Beast of Virtue: Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Natural weapons, Protection and species Qualities for animals, and the reminder to subtract Size from initial Might.
quotes: Remember to subtract the Size of a Beast of Virtue from the initial Might score to get the final Might score.

entries.title: Birds of Nephelococcygia
entries.summary: Describes the cloud regio of Nephelococcygia, how to enter it, and the Inherited Virtues and Flaws of the intelligent birds who live there.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Homing Instinct, Keen Vision, Lightning Reflexes.
an Intelligence + Magic Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9

entries.title: Powers of the Birds of Nephelococcygia
entries.summary: The set of Greater Powers available to Birds of Nephelococcygia, each given with its Hermetic guideline breakdown.

entries.title: Bird Flight
entries.summary: Flight is natural to these birds and needs no roll under normal conditions; difficult conditions call for a flying roll.
quotes: he has an initiative of Qik + Athletics (flying) for this maneuver
a roll (Dexterity + Athletics(flying) + stress die) may be required to take to the air

entries.title: The Magical Lineages of Cats
entries.summary: Introduces the three cat lineages descended from familiars of the Founders, whose magical features breed almost true.

entries.title: Cat Character Template
entries.summary: A worked template showing how to build a magical cat character from the mundane stats and magical additions.
quotes: Cats may only have 10 points of Qualities
Might divided by 5, rounded up

entries.title: Cats as Example
entries.summary: Explains that the cat section is a model for building power lists for other species, borrowing powers and following the same guidelines.

entries.title: Black Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the Black Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: White Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the White Lineage and lists its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: Tortoiseshell Lineage of Cats
entries.summary: Describes the Tortoiseshell Lineage, its rare males, and its common Virtues or Qualities, Flaws or Inferiorities, and powers.

entries.title: Cat Magical Powers
entries.summary: Each purchase of a Greater or Lesser Magical Power Quality gives a cat one power chosen from the lists.
quotes: Players designing cats select one magical power for each purchase of the Greater Magical Power or Lesser Magical Power Qualities.

entries.title: Cats' Greater and Lesser Powers
entries.summary: Rules for the spell-level cost, Penetration Score, Might cost and Initiative Bonus of cat powers.
quotes: A Penetration Score = Might of the cat (5 x the cost of the power) + the cat's Penetration Bonus.
The Initiative Bonus for a Lesser Power is equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude x 2).

entries.title: Warder's Walk
entries.summary: A cat power letting several cats combine their other powers in a ritual to penetrate Magic Resistance, at the risk of a fatal botch as more cats join.
quotes: It is a variant of Wizard's Communion.

entries.title: Black Cat Wards
entries.summary: Describes the ward powers Black Lineage cats use, singly or in procession, to protect a home or settlement against minor faeries and demons.

entries.title: Personal Magical Powers for Cats
entries.summary: Rules for the Initiative bonus, spell-level cost and Penetration Score of personal powers for cats.
quotes: An Initiative bonus equal to the cat's Quickness – (Magnitude /2).

entries.title: Dragons and Dragon-kind
entries.summary: Distinguishes serpents, drakes, worms and true dragons, and advises that the largest dragons exceed what the rules can represent and need innovative plans to defeat.

entries.title: Dragons as Characters
entries.summary: Weak dragons can be built with the magical character rules as grogs, companions or magus-equivalents, while non-player dragons need not be strictly balanced.

entries.title: Dragon Concept
entries.summary: Base Characteristics, Size, required Virtues and suggested Virtues and Flaws when designing a dragon or dragon-kin.
quotes: Dragons and their kin have base Characteristics of 0, and 7 points to spend on improving Characteristics (like human characters).

entries.title: Dragon Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Guidance on which seasons suit serpents and dragons and on giving combat opponents a good Brawl.

entries.title: Dragon Might Score and Qualities
entries.summary: A table of typical Might ranges for each kind of dragon-kin, plus advice on Qualities for breath, gaze and combat statistics.
quotes: A dragon's combat statistics may be improved through liberal use of the Improved Attack, Improved Defense, Improved Damage, and Improved Soak Qualities.

entries.title: Claw and Fang
entries.summary: A table of weapon statistics for dragon claws and teeth, with large versions for dragons bigger than Size +2.
quotes: Dragons larger than Size +2 usually have large claws and/or large teeth.

entries.title: Constriction Attacks (Option)
entries.requires: Being type: Dragon, worm or large serpent
entries.summary: An optional rule for dragons and serpents to constrict smaller victims using the grappling rules, depriving them of air.
quotes: A dragon can only constrict a victim whose Size is less than its own.
a constriction attack has the following weapon statistics: Init 0, Atk +3, Dfn 0, Dam n/a
The victim must make a Stamina check every 30 seconds, that is, every five rounds, or suffer the normal effects of deprivation.

entries.title: Transformed Animals
entries.summary: Distinguishes Transformed Animals, which are Warped by magic and gain no Magic Might, from Beasts of Virtue.

entries.title: Warping of Animals
entries.summary: Animals gain Warping points like people and acquire Flaws and then a Virtue at set Warping Scores.
quotes: Once an animal gains a Warping score of 1 it acquires a Minor Flaw, and it gains another Minor Flaw when its Warping score reaches 3.

entries.title: Warped Livestock (Covenant Hook)
entries.summary: A covenant with Warped animals may farm them for Muto vis, represented by a vis source Boon.

entries.title: Intentionally Warping an Animal
entries.summary: A cage of change is an enchanted device that gives a captive animal Warping points to make it monstrous for harvesting Muto vis.
quotes: the cage gives the captive in the cage 5 Warping Points

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws from Warping
entries.summary: Lists the Supernatural Virtues and Flaws a magically Warped animal may gain, culminating in a Lesser Power at Warping Score 5.
quotes: eventually acquiring a Lesser Power when it reaches a Warping Score of 5

entries.title: Taming Mundane Beasts
entries.summary: Gives mundane beasts an effective Might for taming purposes and notes that Gift penalties apply because taming is social.
quotes: mundane beasts have an effective (Animal) Might of 1 + 2 times Confidence Score

entries.title: Transylvanian Dragons: Realms, Detection and Might
entries.summary: Explains that local dragons belong to the Infernal or Magic realm, how realm-specific Intellego Vim spells tell them apart, and the Might ranges used for weak, typical, powerful and legendary dragons.
quotes: Intellego Vim spells will indicate which realm a creature is associated with, although each Intellego Vim spell must be realm-specific.
Weak dragons have Infernal or Magic Might Scores between 15 and 30, typical dragons between 30 and 40, and the most powerful dragons have Might scores between 40 and 50.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.74 Dragons

entries.title: Infernal Dragons (aždaje)
entries.summary: Describes aždaje as intelligent Infernal beasts rather than demons, their dominance hierarchy, their ability to pose as Magical dragons if they resist Intellego Vim, and their lairs in corrupted Infernal auras.
quotes: Unlike other Infernal beasts, aždaje are intelligent instead of cunning.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.15 Infernal auras

entries.title: Building a Corrupted Dragon
entries.summary: Explains how to create game statistics for a corrupted dragon, either from Infernal and beast Virtues and Flaws or by adding Infernal Virtues and Flaws to a Magic dragon, which then uses Infernal Might.
quotes: In most cases, a corrupted beast is a tainted version of a mundane beast, and game statistics are created by adding Infernal Virtues and Flaws to the mundane beast's existing statistics.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal pp.77-79
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Multiple Attacks by Multi-Headed Dragons
entries.summary: Sample magical dragon statistics whose bite footnote sets how many attacks a huge creature can make against a single target in one round, scaling with the target's Size.
quotes: he can only attack a specific Size 0 target twice in a single round
For each Size above 0, the dragon can add an additional attack to that target in the same round.

entries.title: Dragon-Born (Magic Kin)
entries.summary: Explains dragon-born human offspring of zmajevi as a type of Magic Kin who buy Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws at character generation and can be identified with Second Sight.
quotes: Dragon-born are another type of Magic Kin

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic p.89 Magic Kin

entries.title: Dragon-Born Statistics
entries.summary: Gives the Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws for dragon-born characters, requires a Personal Power mirroring the dragon parent's powers, and offers example powers.
quotes: Greater Immunity (fire)
A dragon-born character receives a Personal Power

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic Realm p.41 Personal powers

gated.title: Magic humans
gated.intro: Giants, magic kin and transformed humans.

entries.title: How Big is a Giant?
entries.summary: A table of approximate height and weight for each Size, noting that Size determines height and weight rather than the reverse.
quotes: a character's height and weight are determined by his Size Characteristic, not the other way round

entries.title: Giants in Combat
entries.summary: An optional rule of thumb giving giants a defensive bonus against scuffling, grappling and disarming by smaller opponents, and notes on Corpus spells against giants.
quotes: a giant gains a special defensive bonus equal to double the difference between its Size and a smaller opponent's

entries.title: Designing Giants
entries.summary: Humanoid beings larger than human size get their Size from the Gigantic Quality.

entries.title: Giant Concept
entries.summary: Story roles and suggested Virtues and Flaws for giants, which use the Magic Human rules with the Gigantic Quality applied after Characteristics.
quotes: Giants should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4.

entries.title: Giant Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Spring giants suffer child-like Characteristic penalties and language Abilities must be bought with the giant's season experience.

entries.title: Giant Might and Qualities
entries.summary: All giants take the Major Quality Gigantic, repeated for larger Sizes, which drives the Might needed.
quotes: All giants must take the Major Quality, Gigantic; giants larger than Size +2 should take it more than once.

entries.title: Giant Finishing Touches
entries.summary: Giants use clubs, with combat statistics computed normally allowing for the Gigantic Quality's effects.

entries.title: Norse Giants and Trolls
entries.requires: Being type: Norse giant or troll
entries.summary: Options for building Norse giants and trolls, including elemental Form affiliations, typical powers and a size-changing rule.
quotes: When the giant reduces its size, its Strength diminishes by 2 and its Quickness improves by 1 for each point of Size reduction.

entries.title: Non-Human Giants
entries.summary: To build oversized elementals, spirits or animals, use the rules for that creature type and add the Gigantic Quality.
quotes: simply choose Gigantic as one of the creature's Qualities

entries.title: Spirit Votary (Virtue and Character Type)
entries.summary: A Free Supernatural Virtue making the character a Mythic Companion who must take Spiritual Pact plus further supernatural Virtues and the Pagan Flaw.
quotes: A Spirit Votary is required to take the Spiritual Pact Virtue (see below), along with either three Minor Supernatural Virtues or one Major Supernatural Virtue.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: True Lineages p.103 Blood of Heroes

entries.title: Magic Kin
entries.summary: Introduces magic kin lineages that can be used as templates for magic characters, each with Inherited Virtues and Common Flaws to take at character creation.
quotes: that characters designed to belong to that family should strongly consider taking during character creation

entries.title: Atlanteans
entries.summary: Template for ocean-dwelling Atlantean characters with water-based Inherited Virtues, an exile Flaw and powers working over water-ways.
quotes: Other water creatures will only obey a summons if a Presence + Leadership roll against an Ease Factor of 6 + Creature Size is successfully made.

entries.title: Flame Dancers
entries.summary: Template for people possessed by the power of fire, with fire-related powers and compulsions.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Let the Bonfire Burn, Personal Power: Endurance of the Flame Dancer

entries.title: Forgotten Gods
entries.summary: Template for old gods who survive in living form, built around a Focus or Greater Power describing their sphere of influence.
quotes: As characters, they should take a Greater Power or Focus Power that describes this influence.

entries.title: Loamwalkers
entries.summary: Template for tree-spirits living in human shape, with powers to travel between trees and change between tree and human form.
quotes: Common Flaws: Dark Secret (Loamwalker), Essential Flaw (minor): Antisocial (Presence), Fear (fire), Baneful Circumstances (must be rooted into the earth)

entries.title: Lost Children
entries.summary: Template for abandoned children who became ageless Magical beings, designed with a child's Size and Characteristic penalties.
quotes: so to play one you should design a character with the Size and Characteristics penalties of a child

entries.title: Men of the Lake
entries.requires: Magic kin: Man of the Lake
entries.summary: Template for sentient lake beings with water powers, a seasonal society and a network of lake regiones.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Drown (see page 137), Personal Power: Simulacrum Form, Ritual Power: Command the Waters, Focus Power: Memory of Water, (Lake) Regio Network.

entries.title: Orphan Born
entries.summary: Template for humans conceived beyond the veil of the spirit world, who can become incorporeal and see spirits.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Incorporeal Form, Personal Power: Ghostly/Physical Form, Second Sight

entries.title: People of the Clouds
entries.requires: Magic kin: Person of the Clouds
entries.summary: Template for sky-sailors who command the wind and can fly or sail ships through the air.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Sail the Wind

entries.title: The Stoneskinned
entries.summary: Template for people of living rock whose stone powers scale with age or Might and who turn to stone in daylight.
quotes: These stats are Init +X, Atk +2X, Dfn +X, Dam +2X, where X is either the character's (Might Score / 5) or his (age / 10).

entries.title: Warders of Mystery
entries.summary: Template for the society of Auditores who keep magic secret, with a power to perceive distant places through Arcane Connections.
quotes: Inherited Virtues: Greater Power: Perceive the Distant Truths

entries.title: Drowned Men
entries.summary: Drowned Men are sailors who passed through a magical regio and returned as creatures of Magic.

entries.title: Drowned Men Characters
entries.summary: Drowned Men must take the Transformed (Being) Virtue and commonly have a sea Flaw, Greater Immunity (drowning) and the Servant of the Ocean Flaw.

entries.title: Planning for Drowning
entries.summary: A character can try to become a Drowned Man by contacting and bargaining with a powerful water entity before surrendering to the water, using two rolls.
quotes: Determine Contact Method: Int + Magic Lore + Stress die vs Ease Factor of 12
Negotiation for Power: Int + Bargain + Stress Die vs Ease Factor of 6 + Might / 5

entries.title: Burned and Buried Men
entries.summary: A person might be saved from fire or burial by a magical creature of Ignem or Terram and gain Virtues like a Drowned Man.

entries.title: Designing Revenants
entries.summary: Revenants are usually Spring or Summer Magic Humans with the No Fatigue and Improved Soak Qualities to reflect their resilience.
quotes: They should be designed according to the rules for Magic Humans in Chapter 4: Magic Characters.

entries.title: Magi in Final Twilight
entries.summary: A magus entering Final Twilight may rarely become a Magical being, with Might set by guideline ranges or formulas tied to an Art or Ability.
quotes: The Might Score of a magus Transformed by Twilight should generally be around 20 to 40.

related.text: Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults p.24 Great Beasts

entries.title: Laying Ghosts and Revenants the Mundane Way
entries.summary: Non-magical methods of putting restless ghosts and vengeful revenants to rest, such as completing unfinished tasks, giving a proper burial, or exhuming, beheading and blessing the grave of a revenant.

entries.title: Ghosts (Apparitions, Shades, Spectres)
entries.summary: Describes the kinds of Magical ghost (apparitions, shades and spectres), how each remembers its life, what ties it to the world and how it can be laid to rest.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, page 36

entries.title: Ghosts as Characters
entries.summary: Ghosts are built as spirits with the Magic Spirit Virtue, and the ability to take material form is treated as a supernatural power that not every ghost has.
quotes: are spirits with no true material form and must have the Magic Spirit special Virtue

entries.title: Designing a Ghost: Concept
entries.summary: Steps for building a ghost: choose a Flaw as its worldly tie, generate Characteristics as for a human, give it Magic Spirit and a Magical Social Status, and drop Virtues and Flaws that no longer apply.
quotes: All ghosts should have the special Virtue, Magic Spirit

entries.title: Designing a Ghost: Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Guidance on which character Season to use for apparitions, shades and spectres according to how much of their living knowledge they retain.
quotes: should usually be designed as Autumn characters.

entries.title: Daimons: General Rules, Aspects and Pacts
entries.summary: Explains how Daimons act on Earth through Aspects, how they are Banished rather than killed, and how theurgists conjure them to provide powers and services.
quotes: A Daimon also does not respond in person — it sends an Aspect of its spirit.
binding or destroying an Aspect has no effect on the Daimon itself
Daimons are never killed or incapacitated by physical combat

entries.title: Daimons
entries.summary: Daimons, the Named Spirits, remain in the Magic Realm and act on Earth only through short-lived Aspects with their own Might, which are constant Arcane Connections to the parent.
quotes: A Daimon is a permanent resident of the Magic Realm and cannot enter the material world; instead, it creates an Aspect as its agent on Earth.

entries.title: The Named Spirits (Daimons and Aspects)
entries.summary: Daimons draw power from True Names and act in the world through Aspects, each of which is built as its own spirit with separate statistics.
quotes: Each Aspect of a Daimon should be created as if it were an independent spirit.

entries.title: Spirits as Characters
entries.summary: Spirits are incorporeal, immortal beings that cannot affect or be sensed by matter without powers or magic, communicating through Silent Speech, and take the Magic Spirit Virtue.

entries.title: Spirit Concept
entries.summary: How to set Characteristics for spirits, that Size is meaningless until a spirit takes physical form, and that all spirits have the Magical Air Flaw.
quotes: For plants and spirits of non-living objects, assume that all Characteristics begin at zero and apply 7 characteristic points in the usual fashion.

entries.title: Taxonomy of the Invisible World
entries.summary: Defines the terms spirit, genius, animus, Daimon and Airy Spirit used for the rules in this chapter.

entries.title: Spirit Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Which seasons suit different kinds of spirits and why spirits often take Reduced Abilities.

entries.title: Spirit Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Spirits need no Quality to be incorporeal or immortal, but need Powers to be seen or to affect the world, so most of their Qualities go to Powers.

entries.title: Powers of the Spirits
entries.summary: Introduces common spirit powers, which must penetrate Magic Resistance, with Ritual-like powers permanently reducing the spirit's Might.
quotes: Naturally, any power that affects another being must penetrate its Magic Resistance.

entries.title: Spirits as a Source of Vis
entries.summary: Explains how much raw vis a spirit contains, when it can be distilled after the spirit is slain, and the vis from corporeal bodies and Presence.
quotes: typically 1 pawn of an appropriate Form per magnitude of their Might

entries.title: Spirit Power: Control Human
entries.summary: A spirit power to direct a human, who may resist with an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor set by the spirit's Might.
quotes: To break free, the target makes an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor equal to 9 + magnitude of spirit's Might.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Donning the Corporeal Veil
entries.summary: A spirit power to create and animate a physical body that shares the spirit's statistics but is limited in Size.
quotes: The body created with this power has the same physical statistics as the spirit, but can have a maximum Size of +1.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Eidolon
entries.summary: A spirit power creating an illusory form visible and audible to material beings.
quotes: Creates an illusionary form that is visible and audible to material beings.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Manifestation
entries.summary: A spirit power to take control of plants or animals by touch, with the amount controlled set by the Might points spent.
quotes: For an extra 2 Might points, a group of ten standard creatures or plants (or the equivalent mass) can be controlled.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Material Anchor
entries.summary: A ritual-like spirit power forming an Arcane Connection to a person or place, or making an object a connection to the spirit, with cost set by duration.
quotes: If the connection is to last for hours or days, then it costs just 1 point; a connection that lasts for weeks or months costs 2 points; years or decades costs 3 points; and indefinite Arcane Connections cost 4 points.

entries.title: Spirit Power: Presence
entries.summary: A spirit power giving awareness of a domain whose size depends on its Might, doubling Might for Tether Strength and yielding yearly vis.
quotes: The area controlled by the spirit can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of vis of an appropriate Form

entries.title: Spirit Power: Regio
entries.summary: A ritual-like power for a spirit with Presence to form a Magic regio with one or more layers of rising aura strength.
quotes: each additional layer has an aura 2 points stronger than the previous layer, up to a maximum of 10

entries.title: Spirit Power: Stasis
entries.summary: A ritual-like power making a Magic-aura area timeless, so residents' aging points become Warping points and long-term residents cannot leave the aura.
quotes: However, any aging points are applied to the character as Warping points instead.

entries.title: Florae and Fauni
entries.summary: Airy Spirits attached to individual plants and animals, with typical Magic Might range and powers for designing them.
quotes: Most fauni and florae possess Cunning rather than Intelligence.

entries.title: Spirits of the Elements
entries.summary: Airy Spirits tied to individual non-living natural objects, with Might scaling by the object's size and importance and differing outlooks by elemental Form.
quotes: A spirit of an element can be present in any matter that is still in its natural form

entries.title: Imagines, Spirits of Sensation
entries.summary: Airy Spirits embodying sensory species, with Imaginem Might and powers that replicate effects matching their sensation.
quotes: The weakest of these spirits represents a specific incidence of a species, whereas those of Might 10 or more represent more-general qualities.

entries.title: Eidolons, Spirits of Emotions
entries.summary: Spirits of emotion created by humans in contact with strong magic; their Might derives from Personality Flaws or Traits and they can be summoned through an Arcane Connection to a person feeling the emotion.
quotes: Otherwise, the spirit has a Might equal to (5 x Personality Trait).

entries.title: Spell Spirits
entries.summary: Theurgists can summon spirits whose only power duplicates a specific spell or Form; the summoning duration sets how long the spirit attends.
quotes: A spell spirit has a Might at least equal to the level of the spell

entries.title: Spirits of Place, Genii Loci
entries.summary: The most powerful Airy Spirits, bound to a locus (a place) rather than an object, with typical powers and a protective relationship to everything in the locus.
quotes: Further, all genii loci possess the Ways of the (Land) Virtue.

entries.title: Jinn
entries.requires: Being type: Jinn (Magic, Faerie or Infernal)
entries.summary: A variety of genii loci from desert lands that can align to Magic, Faerie or Infernal Realms, share a bargain-binding Malediction, and can temporarily transfer their locus.
quotes: it is bound to the agreed terms unless its partner reneges first

entries.title: Lugra, Spirits of Hardship
entries.summary: Parasitic spirits of life's hardships that afflict randomly chosen hosts, with typical Control Human and Mastery powers.

entries.title: Spirits and Hermetic Magic
entries.summary: How Hermetic magi summon and control Airy Spirits with Rego, and the extra requirements for summoning a Daimon's Aspect, with theurgist advantages.
quotes: the spell of the non-theurgist must have a base level equal to twice the Daimon's Might

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapters 4, 8 and 9

entries.title: New Spirit Spells and Spell Guidelines
entries.summary: General rule that spells to summon, perceive or control spirits must penetrate the spirit's Magic Might, with notes on controlling a Daimon's Aspect.
quotes: All spells to summon, perceive, or control a spirit must penetrate its Magic Might.

entries.title: Intellego (Form) Spirit Guidelines
entries.summary: Intellego guidelines for sensing supernatural creatures whose Might is aligned to a Form, graded by minimum Might.
quotes: Sense a supernatural creature of Might 30 or above with a Might associated with the Form.

entries.title: Rego (Form) Spirit Guidelines
entries.summary: Rego guidelines for controlling and summoning Airy Spirits tied to a Form; an Arcane Connection is always needed to summon.
quotes: Control an Airy Spirit of (Form).
Summon an Airy Spirit of (Form).

entries.title: Rego Vim Spirit Guidelines
entries.summary: Rego Vim guidelines for controlling or summoning Airy Spirits of a Realm, and a general guideline for summoning a Daimon's Aspect as a Ritual.
quotes: Summon an Aspect of a Daimon if (level + 4 magnitudes) equals or exceeds twice its Might. (Ritual)

entries.title: Spirits and Non-Hermetic Magic (Goetic Arts)
entries.summary: Summary of the four Goetic Arts used by non-Hermetic sorcerers to summon, drain, bind and command spirits, and which Realms each is aligned to.
quotes: There are four Goetic Arts — namely Summoning, Ablating, Binding, and Commanding

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, Chapter 11: Ars Goetia

entries.title: Characters Touched by Spirits of Place
entries.summary: Ways characters can gain powers from long exposure to a genius loci: birth Virtues and Flaws, Grant powers, possession, bargains and pacts, communion for Mystery initiation, and Warping.
quotes: Major bargains may constitute a pact (granting the Spiritual Pact Virtue)

entries.title: Elementals: Rarefication
entries.summary: Describes what elementals are (pure elemental matter given pseudo-life by magic, not truly alive) and how rarefication forms one, including accidental and spontaneous formation in Magic auras. Once formed an elemental does not age, eat or fall ill.
quotes: The process of forming an elemental is called rarefication.
raw elemental matter possessing a Warping Score of 5 may spontaneously rarefy into an elemental

entries.title: Elementals and Might
entries.summary: How elementals regain spent Might: slowly while resting in a suitable Magic aura, or immediately by consuming vis.
quotes: An elemental does not replenish its Might Pool every day, but instead only recovers Might Points when resting in a Magic aura of no less than (its Might Score / 5)
5 Might Points for every pawn of vis associated with the same Form as its Might, or 2 Might Points for every pawn of vis associated with any other Art.

entries.title: Size, Might and Characteristics of Elementals
entries.summary: A table giving an elemental's Size and its eight Characteristics for each Might score from 1 to 50, used when designing a new elemental.
quotes: The Size of an elemental is dependent on the Might chosen for it, and the Might of an elemental also determines its typical Characteristics.

alsoIn.title: Size, Might, and Characteristics of Elementals

entries.title: Magic and Elementals
entries.summary: How Hermetic magic creates, controls, wards and destroys elementals, and how botched spells or lab activity involving an elemental Form in a Magic aura can accidentally rarefy one.
quotes: Ritual Creo spells can create elementals, and they may be controlled using Rego magic.
The production of an elemental is a potential consequence of any botched spell or lab activity involving an elemental Form while in a Magic aura.

entries.title: Elemental Combat
entries.summary: Elementals cannot be wounded in the usual way: each blow also drains their Might Pool, they go inanimate at zero Might, and pieces knocked off in combat carry vis that can be collected or reabsorbed.
quotes: each wound also reduces the elemental's Might Pool by a number of points equal to the Wound Penalty
An Incapacitating Wound removes 5 Might points, just like a Heavy Wound.
a number of pawns equal to ((total Wound penalty /5) – the number of pawns already lost)

entries.title: Elemental Powers
entries.summary: Every elemental has a power from its elemental matter and a power describing its natural attack, plus usually one more. Its natural attack costs no Might points, so its Penetration is typically its Might.
quotes: the elemental does not need to spend Might points for this attack, meaning that its Penetration for this is typically equal to its Might.

entries.title: Earth Elementals (Genomi)
entries.summary: What earth elementals can be rarefied from, how the quantity of raw material limits their Might, how they behave and attack, and which weapons can hurt them.
quotes: Only bludgeoning weapons such as hammers, maces, or axes can damage an earth elemental
They may be rarefied from any large concretion of earth that has not been worked by human hands

entries.title: Earth Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Crush power every earth elemental has (pinning and breaking equipment) and optional powers such as The Red Touch and Slake Thirst, with their spell-equivalent guidelines.
quotes: All earth elementals have the following power:

entries.title: Water Elementals (Lymphae)
entries.summary: What water elementals can be rarefied from, their temperament, movement and attacks, and how weapons and fire affect them.
quotes: A water elemental's attacks only inflict Scuffle damage
Only naturally occurring liquids can produce elementals, typically of salt or fresh water.

entries.title: Water Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Drown power every water elemental has and optional powers such as Chill Touch and Sight of the River, with their spell-equivalent guidelines.
quotes: All water elementals have the following power:

entries.title: Air Elementals (Zephyri)
entries.summary: What air elementals can be rarefied from, their restless nature, perception and movement, and their immunity to weapons.
quotes: Any air under the open sky or any natural weather phenomenon can produce a zephyrus.

entries.title: Air Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Sufficiale suffocation power every air elemental has, including the contested Quickness + Athletics roll to escape, plus optional powers such as Dissolution and Jupiter's Touch.
quotes: All air elementals have the following power:
Compare Quickness + Athletics stress rolls of the victim and the elemental (using Might/5 for the elemental's Athletics), the highest wins.

entries.title: Fire Elementals (Phlegethi)
entries.summary: What fire elementals can be rarefied from, how they feed, move across flammable surfaces and jump gaps, and how weapons and water affect them.
quotes: It may also jump a gap of nonflammable surface (such as bare rock) up to a width equal to its Magic Might in feet.
Larger sources of water quench the elemental's body, inflicting "wounds" as if it were fire damage

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.67

entries.title: Fire Elemental Sample Powers
entries.summary: The Burn power every fire elemental has (damage from a stress die plus its current Might pool) and optional powers such as Fascination and Heat of the Searing Forge.
quotes: All fire elementals have the following power:
takes damage equal to a stress die plus the entity's current Might pool

entries.title: New Elementals Spells and Spell Guidelines
entries.summary: Spell guidelines for creating, converting, controlling and destroying elementals using the elemental Forms.
quotes: Create an elemental from a base amount of elemental matter (Ritual)
Completely control an elemental

entries.title: Designing Elementals
entries.summary: Introduction to building an elemental character as a Magic Thing, with its inherited Virtues and Flaws.
quotes: the general principles can be applied to use an elemental as the starting point for a magic character

entries.title: Elemental Concept and Characteristics
entries.summary: How an elemental's Size and element determine its Characteristics, which Characteristics cannot be negative for each element, and the Size adjustment applied to Quickness and Strength.
quotes: make the usual adjustment from Size, subtracting Size from Quickness and adding twice Size to Strength.

entries.title: Elemental Season and Abilities
entries.summary: Elementals are normally Spring characters and must buy Brawl and Athletics (or Swim for water) to a score tied to their Might, using Improved Abilities if experience runs short.
quotes: Elementals are almost always Spring characters

entries.title: Elemental Might and Qualities
entries.summary: Elemental Might is set by the amount of matter it formed from and fixes its Size, with fixed free Qualities and an obligatory Greater Power for its element.
quotes: Every increase in magnitude of Might (as if it were a spell) adds three to the Size.

gated.title: Faeries
gated.intro: Faerie characters: Glamour, Pretenses and their powers.

entries.title: Creatures of Faerie: Roles and Pretenses
entries.summary: General rules for faeries: they are bound to story roles they cannot break, their physical attacks ignore Magic Resistance, and they have Pretenses rather than Abilities, which a skilled observer may detect with a Perception + Awareness roll.
quotes: Despite this, their physical attacks are not blocked by Magic Resistance, including the Parma Magica.
Faeries have Pretenses instead of Abilities.
may make a Perception + Awareness roll against an Ease Factor of 12

entries.title: Faerie Virtues and Flaws (Cognizance, Wards, Faerie Sight and Speech)
entries.summary: Explains the faerie-specific traits used to build faeries: regeneration without fatigue, degrees of Cognizance, Faerie Sight, Faerie Speech, and Traditional and Sovereign Wards that harm or exclude a faerie.
quotes: Assume that the object acts as a source of damage with an intensity of +6.
Direct contact with a sovereign ward destroys the body of a faerie, removing it from the scenario.
The faerie cannot regenerate Might points in the presence of a traditional ward.

entries.title: Faerie Lore and What a Character Knows
entries.summary: Sidebar ruling that the Faerie Lore Ability covers understanding, bargaining with and predicting faeries regardless of whether a character uses the book's framework, and that no perspective is at a disadvantage in play.
quotes: The Faerie Lore Ability quantifies the character's capacity to understand the motives of, bargain with, and predict the actions of faeries.

entries.title: Cognizance: Incognizant, Narrow and High
entries.summary: Classifies faeries by how well they understand their own need for human vitality (incognizant, narrowly cognizant, highly cognizant), which governs their memory, pain, planning and ability to change themselves.
quotes: All faeries require human vitality, and seek it instinctively.

related.text: Chapter 3: Faerie Characters, Cognizance Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Glamour: Rules Instead of a Soul
entries.summary: Describes glamour as the set of rules tied to a faerie's role; a faerie cannot break them and fades if it stops fulfilling its role, and it grows stronger by taking part in stories.
quotes: Faeries cannot break their glamour.

entries.title: Faerie Bodies and Spiritual Anchors
entries.summary: A faerie builds its body from incidental matter around a spiritual anchor; the anchor holds the faerie's vis and lets it rebuild after its body is destroyed, and pain depends on cognizance.
quotes: Incognizant faeries feel pain when their bodies are damaged, narrowly cognizant faeries must appear to, and highly cognizant faeries suffer pain only if they wish to.
The spiritual anchor, filled with glamour, is the vis that magi hunt so earnestly.

entries.title: Faerie Ownership and Stolen Goods
entries.summary: Items a faerie owns are part of its glamour and revert to incidental matter, with any vis vanishing, if taken against its will; its possessions and mortal belongings with Arcane Connections matter to faeries.
quotes: All of a faerie's possessions, if generated from glamour, are Arcane Connections to the faerie until it changes its role.

entries.title: Faerie Taboos
entries.summary: Each faerie has mandatory and forbidden actions; a human who breaks one offends the faerie and owes redress, and may take this as the origin of a Story Flaw.
quotes: A human breaking the taboos of a faerie offends it, and owes it redress.

entries.title: Pretenses and Noticing Them
entries.summary: Faeries mimic human Abilities with Pretenses, which cost no Might and need no Concentration; masters of the imitated Ability can notice the deception with a Perception + Awareness check against a stated difficulty.
quotes: Pretenses do not cost Might, and faeries use them without Concentration
This requires a Perception + Awareness check of 12 – the Ability score the faerie is pretending to have.

related.text: Chapter 3: Faerie Characters, Pretense: Faerie Abilities
