entries.title: Open Body: Arcane Connections to Faeries
entries.summary: Speaking to, eating the food of, bleeding near, or having sex with a faerie opens a human to its glamour and creates a temporary Arcane Connection with a stated Penetration multiplier; pregnancy by a faerie creates a longer-lasting one.
quotes: Speaking to a faerie creates an Arcane Connection to that faerie with a Penetration multiplier of 2 that endures until the conversation ends.
A character whose blood is taken or tasted by a faerie has an Arcane Connection to that Faerie with a Penetration multiplier of 3 until the wound heals.
Intercourse with a faerie creates an Arcane Connection to that faerie with a Penetration multiplier of 4 during the intercourse.

related.text: Chapter 3: Faerie Characters, Traditional and Sovereign Wards

entries.title: No Numerical System for Vitality
entries.summary: Sidebar stating that the game tracks no points of vitality: faeries do not spend it to survive or advance, they simply always want more.
quotes: There is no numerical system for vitality.

entries.title: Vitality: How Faeries Feed
entries.summary: Describes the ways faeries harvest human vitality (roused emotion, art, offerings, theft, border crossings, blood and flesh, violence), which the storyguide uses to decide what a faerie wants and does.

entries.title: Designing Faerie Characters: Sequence of Choices
entries.summary: Overview of the order of decisions for creating a faerie: player or non-player, power level, Might, physical form, cognizance, role, powers and vulnerabilities.
quotes: Faeries are designed through a series of choices.

entries.title: Faerie Characters: PC or NPC
entries.summary: Non-player faeries may be more powerful than new player characters and need not balance Virtues and Flaws; the bestiary uses these rules as examples but troupes may design more informally.
quotes: Non-player characters do not need to balance their Virtues and Flaws

entries.title: Faerie Level of Power
entries.summary: A player faerie should be about as powerful as a companion or magus, and the troupe should agree on the design so that it does not reduce others' enjoyment.
quotes: approximately as powerful as a companion or magus

entries.title: Faerie Virtues, Flaws and Pretense Points
entries.summary: A player faerie replacing a companion or magus gets a limited allotment of Virtues balanced by Flaws, and a pool of Pretense points set by the average magus age; inherent Abilities of the physical form must be bought first.
quotes: 1 free, then up to 20 points of Virtues paid for with Flaws at 2 Virtues per Flaw.
(average age of magus player characters – 5) + 120 points
which gives 360 points of Pretences

entries.title: Faerie Monarchs
entries.summary: Design benchmark for how mighty a faerie ruler must be to threaten senior magi and why a court helps.
quotes: it requires a Faerie Might score of around 60, and the Penetration Pretense

entries.title: Required Virtues and Flaws for Faeries
entries.summary: Every faerie character needs a Might score, physical form, level of cognizance, Social Interaction Virtue and a taboo; innate powers can be traded away as Flaws.
quotes: A character must have a Might score, a physical form, a level of cognizance, a Social Interaction Virtue, and a taboo.

entries.title: Faerie Might Score and Might Points
entries.summary: Sets a starting Might score for player faeries, gives innate Magic Resistance equal to Might, and explains that Might Points are spent on powers and recover steadily over a day; notes that Might varies widely with role.
quotes: Player characters begin with a Faerie Might score of 5
Faerie Might gives the character innate Magic Resistance equal to its Might Score.
Faeries have Might Points equal in number to their Might score, which they spend to activate their powers.

entries.title: Quick Start Guideline (Faerie Characters)
entries.summary: Sidebar giving a fast recipe for a companion-level faerie: a stated Might, Characteristics and Pretence points, a short list of Virtues, free choices and a Traditional Ward Flaw.
quotes: has a Faerie Might of 10
360 Points of Pretences: Spend them exactly like Ability points.

entries.title: Faerie Physical Form: Ageing and Fatigue
entries.summary: Explains what a faerie body is and its advantages: no ageing or Decrepitude unless a Flaw says otherwise, no Fatigue, and great difficulty in dying.
quotes: Faeries cannot age or suffer Decrepitude unless they have a Flaw.

entries.title: Equipment Without Encumbrance
entries.summary: A faerie carries traditional props of its role without Encumbrance and can reconstitute a lost prop for no Might in a round.
quotes: Reconstituting a prop costs no Might, and requires a single round.

entries.title: Faerie Regeneration and Rebuilding a Body
entries.summary: Faeries heal by cognizance level, and a faerie killed before humans rebuilds a body in a time set by its Might and the local aura; memory and role changes after rebuilding depend on cognizance.
quotes: The time taken to regenerate equals the faster of the Faerie Might Score in months or Faerie Might Score / Aura (as modified by the Realm Interaction Table) in months.

entries.title: Scale of Typical Might Scores
entries.summary: Sidebar table giving descriptive Might bands from ordinary creatures to earth-shaking figures with example bestiary faeries at each level.
quotes: | 1–10 | An ordinary creature of a realm. |

entries.title: Permanent Death of Faeries
entries.summary: Lists what kills a faerie permanently: destroyed Might Score, miracles, Infernal agents, use of the vis in its anchor, and antithetical things for incognizant faeries with a Sovereign Ward.
quotes: A faerie whose Might Score is destroyed dies permanently.

entries.title: Magic Resistance Against Faeries
entries.summary: Faerie bodies and props are not blocked by Parma Magica or other Magic Resistance, though wards targeting the faerie's material or spiritual nature work, and powers with a Might cost and a Range beyond Personal are generally resisted.
quotes: Faerie bodies, and the other props created by the same process, are not, however, blocked by the Parma Magica or other forms of Magic Resistance.
The powers of faeries that have Might costs and ranges greater than Personal are, in most cases, opposed by Magic Resistance.

entries.title: Faerie Human and Animal Forms
entries.summary: How to build Characteristics for humanoid and animal-form faeries, and how animal-form player faeries swap Cunning for Intelligence as a free Virtue.
quotes: A humanoid faerie has 7 points with which to buy Characteristics
This is a Free Virtue.

related.text: Realms of Power: Magic, Book of Mundane Animals
Houses of Hermes: Mystery Cults pp.38-43

entries.title: Hybrid Forms and Natural Weapons
entries.summary: Hybrid forms are human forms with animal elements that are cosmetic or Minor Virtues; faeries' natural weapons use Brawl and a table of Init, Atk, Dfn and Dmg values and need no Virtue.
quotes: This uses the Brawl Ability and the statistics on the following table.
Having natural weapons does not, in itself, require a Virtue.

entries.title: Glamorous, Immaterial Forms
entries.summary: Immaterial faeries are invisible and pass through solid objects but must take on matter to move things; design them as the physical body they don, with the Intangible Flesh Flaw.
quotes: Immaterial faeries are invisible to those without magical aid, and can pass through solid objects.

entries.title: Faerie Size
entries.summary: Humanoid faeries choose a Size with required Strength and Quickness adjustments; extreme sizes need troupe scrutiny, and nonhuman characters adjust Characteristics only if they deviate more than one from their base Size.
quotes: Characters outside the range of Size +2 to –3 are difficult to accommodate in sagas, and should be carefully scrutinized by the Troupe.
Characters deviating from their base size by 1 do not change Characteristics, but those deviating by more than 1 are adjusted as indicated by the table above.

entries.title: Faerie Social Interaction Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Faeries take Social Interaction Virtues and Flaws that cover only dealings with humans and replace Social Status Virtues; with other faeries a player faerie is treated as a representative of its human companions.
quotes: govern only their interaction with humans and replace Social Status Virtues

entries.title: Faerie Cognizance in Character Design
entries.summary: A faerie's cognizance shapes its goals and limits how it can develop new powers: low-cognizance faeries do not consciously improve, middling ones transform predictably, and highly cognizant ones can change roles between scenes.
quotes: Characters of low cognizance do not consciously attempt to improve their statistics during the saga.

entries.title: Unspecialized Role (Pretenses for Martial, Arcane and Academic Abilities)
entries.summary: Sidebar ruling that faeries can have Pretenses for Martial, Arcane and Academic Abilities without the Virtues humans need, though professionals quickly detect the fraud.
quotes: Faeries do not require the Virtues that allow characters to have Martial, Arcane, or Academic Abilities to have Pretenses for them.

entries.title: Faerie Taboos: Traditional and Sovereign Wards
entries.summary: Faerie taboos are built from Ward Flaws: a Traditional Ward bars touching the ward, stops Might regeneration and burns the faerie as a damage source, while a Sovereign Ward bars harming the protected person and destroys the faerie's body on touch.
quotes: The faerie cannot regenerate Might points in the presence of a traditional ward.
Assume that the object acts as a source of damage with an intensity of +6.
the faerie may not harm a person or thing that is defended by the ward

entries.title: Folk Charms (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: A faerie with this taboo cannot face folk charms deliberately used against it, whatever the culture; personal charms precious to a human also serve and are Arcane Connections to that human.
quotes: A character with this taboo cannot face folk charms, deliberately used, from any culture

entries.title: Herbs (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: The herbs that repel a faerie depend on its role and the herb's underlying symbolism; identifying the right herb needs Faerie Lore or the ability to read the faerie's glamour.
quotes: The herbs that repel a faerie are based on that faerie's role, so the faerie is unable to vary them, except by changing roles.

entries.title: Iron (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Iron is a common faerie ward, and some faeries refuse to deal with those carrying it, while miners, crafters and urban faeries are often comfortable with it.
quotes: Some faeries refuse to negotiate with humans who carry iron, even if they will not suffer from contact with it

entries.title: Names (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: A character who knows the name of a faerie with this taboo can force it to leave him alone, so powerful faeries use titles and roles instead.
quotes: If a faerie has this taboo, and a character knows its name, the character can force the faerie to leave it alone.

entries.title: Payment or Thanks (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Some faeries must leave human service once paid or thanked, either because the relationship is balanced or their story is complete, and a few then turn on their former employers.
quotes: Some faeries must leave human service if paid or thanked.

entries.title: Places (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Place-based taboos must seriously inconvenience the faerie, for example foreign earth acting as a Traditional Ward, and a Sovereign Ward tying a faerie to its home makes it unsuitable for most player characters.
quotes: Flaws based on places must seriously inconvenience the character.
Characters tied to their home with a Sovereign Ward simply cannot leave, and are unsuitable as player characters in most sagas.

entries.title: Religious Symbols (Faerie Taboo)
entries.summary: Faeries with this taboo flee symbols such as church bells; many powerful faeries also cannot enter the Dominion without God's invitation.
quotes: Many of the most powerful faeries cannot enter the Dominion, because God has not invited them in and they are unable to trespass.

entries.title: Inappropriate Virtues and Flaws for Faeries
entries.summary: Lists which Virtues and Flaws a faerie character may never take (Gift, Hermetic, Divine/Infernal powers, human social status and upbringing) and what to take instead.
quotes: Faeries may not have The Gift, or any Virtue or Flaw specific to Hermetic magi.
If the faerie has a role that makes it appear part of human society, it should take the Infiltrator Virtue.

entries.title: Faeries and Confidence
entries.summary: Faeries have no Confidence scores; the Reputation as Confidence Virtue gives them false Confidence points to back up their Reputations.
quotes: Faeries do not have Confidence scores.
A faerie with this Virtue gains a number of false Confidence points equal to its highest reputation

entries.title: Faerie Personality Flaws
entries.summary: Sets how many Personality Flaws a faerie may take, noting that role-linked Flaws are often required.
quotes: Faeries may have up to three Minor Personality Flaws and one Major Personality Flaw

entries.title: Focus Power
entries.summary: Virtue giving a faerie a themed, spontaneous-style power built from a pool of spell levels, with Might cost and Initiative set by the effect's magnitude.
quotes: The player receives 25 spell levels to spend on this power.
an initiative score of (the character's Quickness – the power's maximum magnitude)

entries.title: Greater Power
entries.summary: Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers designed at character creation, with a reduced Might cost and Initiative penalty compared to Lesser Powers.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 50 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each power has a Might Point cost equal to (the magnitude of the effect / 2)

entries.title: Lesser Power
entries.summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie formulaic spell-like powers; cheaper to acquire than Greater Powers but each use costs more Might and is slower.
quotes: Taking this Virtue gives the character 25 spell levels to spend on these powers
Each effect's Might Point cost is equal to the magnitude of the effect.

entries.title: Personal Power
entries.summary: Minor Virtue giving a faerie a single Personal-range spell-like power designed like a formulaic spell.
quotes: Personal powers must have Personal Range.

entries.title: An Exemplary Catalog of Faerie Powers
entries.summary: General rules for using faerie powers: spending Might for uses, Penetration, wound penalties, running out of Might, and powers across realm boundaries.
quotes: Faeries gain one use of a power each time they spend its cost in Might.
Might Score – (5 x Might Point cost) + Penetration bonus

entries.title: Intricacy Points
entries.summary: Intricacy points let a faerie make a power faster or cheaper in Might, and can be gained from unspent spell levels or the Improved Powers Virtue.
quotes: Every 5 unspent levels equal an intricacy point.

entries.title: Odd Targets and Durations
entries.summary: Allows faerie powers to use Merinita Ranges, Targets and Durations, and defines the Until Duration and dual Durations.
quotes: In this book it is treated as being equivalent to Year, but not requiring a Ritual.

entries.title: Faerie Power Virtue Comparison Table
entries.summary: Table comparing spell levels, effect type, Might cost and Initiative for each faerie power Virtue.
quotes: Qik – maximum magnitude

entries.title: Ritual Power
entries.summary: Major Virtue for ritual-level faerie effects, which cost Might Score as well as Might points whenever they are used.
quotes: All Ritual Powers are at least Level 20, regardless of the actual level of the effect
The Initiative for the power is equal to the character's Quickness – (the magnitude of the effect x 2).

entries.title: Improved Powers
entries.summary: Minor Virtue granting intricacy points to a faerie's powers, or optionally mastery-like abilities for them.
quotes: This Virtue gives the character 5 intricacy points to spend on any of its powers.

entries.title: Constant Powers
entries.summary: Rules for making a Greater, Lesser or Personal Power constant, triggering at every sunrise and sunset.
quotes: costs an additional magnitude

entries.title: Binding Oath
entries.summary: Ritual faerie power enforcing solemn oaths and contracts, warning and then penalising humans who break them.
quotes: Faeries cannot break their oaths

entries.title: Granting Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Ritual faerie powers that impose a Virtue or Flaw (blessing or curse) on a target, permanently at the cost of Might Score or temporarily at the cost of Might points.
quotes: The creature can decide to bestow the Virtue permanently or temporarily.

entries.title: Converting Greater Powers to Lesser Powers
entries.summary: Quick procedure to convert a Greater Power to a Lesser Power by adjusting Might cost and Initiative.
quotes: double the Might cost and quadruple the Initiative penalty of the power

entries.title: Greater and Lesser Faerie Powers
entries.summary: Explains how Lesser Powers compare with Greater Powers and how the powers listed in the book are presented, including the Initiative bonus.
quotes: each use costs twice as much Might as the equivalent Greater Power

entries.title: Craft Magical Trinket
entries.summary: Faerie power that creates a glamour object letting its holder use one Virtue once, at a Might cost depending on the Virtue's size.
quotes: A trinket costs 10 Might points if it invokes a Minor Virtue, and 15 points if it invokes a Major Virtue.

entries.title: Loosely Material
entries.summary: Power letting an immaterial faerie take on a physical body, whose Characteristics and Size are bought with Might points spent on activation.
quotes: For each Might point spent on this power, 5 characteristic points are available to spend on the four physical Characteristics of Strength, Stamina, Dexterity, and Quickness.
A faerie's material body can have any Size up to a maximum of its Presence unless it spends additional Might points on Size.

entries.title: Powers of Transformation
entries.summary: Advice on which faerie power Virtue to use when designing transformation powers, depending on whether specific or varied substances are involved.
quotes: then that is best designed as a Greater Power

entries.title: Focus Powers
entries.summary: Intro to Focus Powers: broad themed effects whose Might cost and Initiative follow the magnitude produced, to be agreed with the troupe.
quotes: Each use of a focus power has a Might Point cost equal to the magnitude of the effect

entries.title: Extended Glamour
entries.summary: Power letting a faerie be aware of everything in its domain, with the domain's size set by the faerie's Might Score, and yielding vis each year.
quotes: The faerie's Might score determines the size of area possible: a Room (5–10 Might), a Structure (15–25 Might), or a standard Boundary (30+ Might).
The area controlled by the faerie can produce a yearly harvest of (Might/10) pawns of vis

entries.title: Power Design: An Example
entries.summary: Worked example of designing faerie powers from Hermetic spells, choosing between Personal, Greater, Lesser and Focus Powers and spending intricacy points.
quotes: Personal powers cost (magnitude/2) points, rounding up

entries.title: Pretense: Faerie Abilities
entries.summary: Explains that faeries use Pretenses in place of Abilities, and that few faeries can teach humans, especially those linked to the dead.
quotes: Some exceptional faeries are able to teach Abilities to humans.

entries.title: Faerie Instructor and Faerie Trainer
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Instructor or Faerie Trainer
entries.summary: Virtues allowing a faerie to teach humans, either by trading stored Abilities or by training with conventional methods.
quotes: The faerie imparts the Ability by trading it for the Ability that the student currently has.

entries.title: Player-Defined Pretenses
entries.summary: Pretenses tied to a faerie's story role rather than a human Ability must be negotiated with the troupe.
quotes: These player-defined pretenses must be negotiated with the troupe.

entries.title: Resistance and Pretenses
entries.summary: Explains that Pretenses guide a faerie's own actions and so are not resisted by Parma Magica, unlike powers or tools aimed at a magus.
quotes: they are not resisted by Parma Magica

entries.title: Player-Defined Pretense Example: Chivalrous Combat
entries.summary: Worked example of negotiating a broad player-defined Pretense with a built-in limitation.

entries.title: Increasing Pretense
entries.summary: How faeries gain Pretense experience by closely involving themselves in humans' stories each season, plus the Virtues and Flaws that change how often this occurs.
quotes: Faeries cannot gain experience from study, training, or practice
During character creation an ostentatious faerie has a Pretense multiplier of 25 instead of 15.

entries.title: Using Abilities On Faeries
entries.summary: Summarises how the common Abilities (Animal Handling, Animal Ken, Folk Ken, Faerie Lore, Language, Teaching and social Abilities) apply to faeries.
quotes: Any Faerie with a score in Faerie Speech can understand any language.
Faeries cannot be taught, since they do not learn by doing.

entries.title: Faerie Advancement Through Change
entries.summary: Overview of what a faerie needs to alter its role and gain powers: cognizance, stored Pretense points, and a creative human collaborator.
quotes: It requires the potential to change within its glamour, represented by the cognizance Virtues.

entries.title: Cognizance and changing a faerie
entries.summary: Describes how incognizant, narrowly cognizant and highly cognizant faeries differ in their understanding of advancement.
quotes: Only highly cognizant faeries understand that they can use human vitality and creativity to tailor their roles in amusing ways.

entries.title: Vitality and changing a faerie's role
entries.summary: Faeries store Pretense points as vitality for changing role, and can consume encased vis to lower the cost of change.
quotes: it reduces the Pretence Cost in the nearby table by 1 for every pawn of vis consumed, to a maximum of the faerie's Might score

entries.title: Creativity: humans helping faeries change
entries.summary: Procedure and table by which a creative human collaborates to change a faerie's glamour, with Ease Factors, Pretense costs and the Virtue and Flaw changes they buy.
quotes: Lose a Virtue or Flaw and gain another of equal value
The Ease Factor should be reduced by 3 if the faerie’s role has drifted away from the folklore of the area

entries.title: Why Isn't My Faerie a Genius At Every Ability?
entries.summary: Explains why starting faerie characters lack great experience, including how and when faeries lose Pretenses.
quotes: Faeries often lose Pretenses.

entries.title: Faerie Blood: Origins and Inheritance
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood
entries.summary: Explains how humans come to have Faerie Blood (through faerie procreation, theft of fertility, or influence on a pregnancy or infant) and how the taint is inherited down the generations.
quotes: Faerie Blood manifests regardless of the number of generations between the first character to bear it and the current generation.

entries.title: Varieties of Faerie Blood
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood
entries.summary: Lists specific kinds of Faerie Blood (bloodcap, brownie, dwarf, ettin, faerie god, ghul, goblin, huldra, nymph, padfoot, satyr, selkie, sidhe, undine), each with its benefit, an enhanced benefit for Faerie Legacy, typical Sympathies, suggested Virtues and Flaws, and appearance.
quotes: Note that this enhanced effect replaces the normal benefit of Faerie Blood, it is not in addition to it.

entries.title: Faerie Powers for the Faerie Blooded
entries.requires: Virtue: Faerie Blood or Strong Faerie Blood (storyguide option)
entries.summary: Optional rule letting a character with Faerie Blood take a restricted list of faerie-only Virtues and Flaws, paying Might costs of their powers in Fatigue rather than Might points.
quotes: instead of spending Might points, the character instead loses 1 Fatigue level for every 5 points (or fraction) of the cost
assume that the character has a Might Score of zero

entries.title: Changelings
entries.summary: Introduces how faeries steal or exchange human infants, leaving behind a faerie child, an ancient faerie or a stock, and what results for the child who is retrieved or who is raised by faeries.

entries.title: Retrieved Changelings
entries.summary: Describes how parents can retrieve a stolen child by tricking the changeling faerie into revealing itself, and what a retrieved child tends to gain, such as Second Sight or Faerie Blood of the kidnappers' variety.

entries.title: Faerie Upbringing (Changelings)
entries.summary: Explains children raised among faeries, who have the Faerie Upbringing Flaw and usually Faerie Blood, and gives the list of Abilities from which a character with this background has an Ability Block.
quotes: Choose any five Abilities from the following list as unavailable to a character with this Flaw: Animal Handling, Charm, Church Lore, Dominion Lore, Etiquette, Folk Ken, Guile, Leadership, Ride, Theology

entries.title: Linked Lives
entries.requires: Exchanged with a troll or trowie changeling
entries.summary: Describes a human whose life is bound to the faerie changeling left in his place, represented by Faerie Blood, possibly Faerie Upbringing, and the Death Prophecy Virtue, with a Faerie Friend or Mistaken Identity relationship.
quotes: that the character can only die if his faerie copy is killed first

entries.title: Milk Brothers
entries.summary: Describes the bond between a human who has shared milk with a gwiber and the creature: the Animal Ken Virtue and the Faerie Friend Flaw rather than Faerie Blood.

entries.title: Nympholepts
entries.summary: Describes mortals taken to live with nymphs for years, who gain Faerie Blood effects plus often a prophetic power such as Premonitions, the Visions Flaw or the Faerie Power of Dream.

entries.title: Giants and their Mothers (Transylvanian giants)
entries.summary: Describes how Transylvanian giants differ from the stock stupid giant: they are refined, arm and armor themselves like knights, and can change Size and shape. Used when designing or running giant faeries.
quotes: many Transylvanian giants can change Size, ranging from Size +2 to +5, with some growing even larger

entries.title: Giants' Mothers
entries.summary: Explains the faerie role of the giant's mother, a sorceress who manages her son, pursues those who defeat him, and adopts a new son if she loses him. Also notes the hereditary hair growing under the tongue of those with giant blood.
quotes: A giant's mother is always a sorceress, and invariably smarter than her son.

entries.title: Faerie Horses
entries.summary: Describes the faerie horse's story role (rescued from a giant's mother's ranch, serves a hero, leaves before the final victory) and the limited foresight a highly cognizant faerie has about other faeries' roles.
quotes: He cannot see into the future, but because he is more cognizant than other participating faeries

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie p.62 Flight

entries.title: Vilas (White Ladies)
entries.summary: Introduces vilas as faerie women who play different roles in each community, to be built from a generic faerie woman and tailored to the role.
quotes: Storyguides designing vilas should use the statistics for a generic faerie woman, and then tailor them to the role that the particular vila plays.

entries.title: Generic Minor Vila (template and power-conversion notes)
entries.summary: Template for a weak generic vila usable as a grog-level antagonist or player character, with notes on buying powers as Greater or Lesser Powers, Personal Powers and a quick-play option for faerie power costs.
quotes: Troupes preferring speed over accuracy should double the Might cost and quadruple the Initiative penalty of the powers given here.

entries.title: Vila Wards (hair, offerings and External Vis)
entries.summary: Describes vila Wards: a strand of hair as a Sovereign Ward, hair as a Minor External Vis source that keeps the vila from truly dying, the Residual Power Virtue, and offerings used as Traditional Wards.
quotes: Vilas often have a Sovereign Ward Flaw for a strand of their own hair.
The hair of a vila is often a Minor External Vis source.

entries.title: Powers Found In Many Roles (vila powers)
entries.summary: Introduces the five groups of powers common to vilas regardless of role: Shapeshifter, Enthralling Voice, Blessing Dance, Cursing Dance and Spirit Away.

entries.title: Vila Shapeshifter Powers
entries.summary: Lists personal shapeshifting powers for vilas that turn them into animals, birds or fish, with Might cost and Initiative by Size and duration; transforming back to human costs the same as the inverse power.
quotes: Faeries retain the power of speech in animal form.
Transform into Human costs the same as the inverse power.

entries.title: Vila Enthralling Voice Powers
entries.summary: Mentem powers modelling a vila's voice: Allure, Enthralling Sound, Enthrallment, Guide, Kiss of Forgetfulness and Steal Judgment, with their costs, durations and the rolls used to resist them.
quotes: Grants a +3 bonus on all rolls that convince or impress others.
A Personality trait roll against an Ease Factor of 9 allows a character to ignore this effect.
Can be resisted with an Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor of 6 for implausible lies.

entries.title: Vila Blessing Dance Powers
entries.summary: Powers a vila uses to grant magical gifts to mortals who dance with her or pass tests: Grant (Major or Minor Virtue) and Grant Puissance in an Ability.
quotes: For every added point spent, a group can be granted +1 on all rolls in a certain situation (combat or court, for example), or one character can be given +3 on a particular Total or roll

entries.title: Vila Cursing Dance Powers
entries.summary: Notes how cursed dances reuse the Enthralling Voice powers and adds Craft Magical Trinket, which makes a dancing circle a cursed magic item with a cost set by the severity of the Flaw.
quotes: This power, which makes the circle a kind of magic item, costs 10 points if the curse is a Minor Flaw, and 15 points if it is a Major Flaw.

entries.title: Spirit Away (vila power)
entries.summary: The power that lets faeries draw mortals into the Faerie realms, with a shortcut for troupes not using the full rules.
quotes: Troupes not using these rules should just assume the attempt succeeds when it suits the story.

entries.title: Role-Specific Vila Powers (customizing by role)
entries.summary: Explains how to build a vila for a story role, balancing added Virtues with Flaws for a player character, and how the Ostentatious and Pretentious Virtues give extra pretense points.
quotes: The first adds 10 times the average age of the PC magi points to the character's pool of pretense points. The second adds 5 times the average age of the PC magi points.

entries.title: Vila Role: Captured Wife
entries.summary: A vila who changes shape and is held by hiding her skin or feathers; the skin can be modeled mechanically as a Skinchanger prop, an External Vis Source or a Sovereign Ward.
quotes: The animal skins can be designed mechanically as the prop for the Skinchanger virtue, as External Vis Source, or as a Sovereign Ward

entries.title: Vila Role: Cloud or Storm Maiden
entries.summary: Powers for cloud and storm vilas: Flight, a Storms Focus power covering Hermetic weather spells up to a level cap, and Guide used to cause travelers to become lost.
quotes: The character has a range of weather-related powers, simulating all Hermetic weather spells of level 25 or less.

entries.title: Vila Role: Cursed Lover
entries.summary: A vila who unknowingly kills her mortal lovers through the Pine Away power, treated as a disease, or through a cursed trinket with a recurring accident motif.
quotes: Simulated as a major disease with an Ease Factor of 9 that causes a Light Wound.

entries.title: Vila Role: Huntress
entries.summary: Additions to the generic vila for a mounted archer, plus the Shake the Earth power which makes characters in 100 paces make a stress roll or fall, with listed modifiers.
quotes: Characters fall unless they make a Quickness – Encumbrance stress roll against an Ease Factor of 10, modified as follows: +2 standing still, +2 on solid stone, +0 moving slowly or on earth, –2 running, –6 on a narrow bridge.

entries.title: Vila Role: Temptress
entries.summary: Powers for a vila who steals young men into woods or waters: Allure, Illusory Home and Pine Away.

entries.title: Vila Role: Water Maiden
entries.summary: Powers for drowned-maiden vilas: Illusory Home and Kiss of the Mermaid, which lets the recipient breathe water until next stepping on dry land.

entries.title: Vila Role: Woodland Maiden
entries.summary: Powers for woodland vilas: Extend Glamor, Guide, a Manifestation Focus power covering Animal and Herbam spells within a level cap in the vila's glamour, and the Transform Victim powers.
quotes: Allows the faerie to simulate any Creo Animal, Rego Animal, Creo Herbam or Rego Herbam spell of level 25 or less in the area of its glamor.

entries.title: Vila Role: Wise Woman
entries.summary: A vila role that mimics a folk witch, with a Healing Focus power that simulates Hermetic healing spells up to a level cap, and a Prophecy power that is only a pretense of foresight.
quotes: Allows the faerie to simulate any Hermetic healing spell up to level 25.

gated.title: Angels and divine beings
gated.intro: Angels and the beings of the Divine.

entries.title: Angelic Powers
entries.summary: The powers every angel possesses: Angelic Mantle to take a material form, Enfolding to protect a soul or body from all harm briefly, and Envisioning to deliver Divine messages in dreams or waking visions.
quotes: All angels possess the following powers:
An angel may also Enfold a person's body (costing 10 Might points)

entries.title: Creatures of the Divine: General Rules
entries.summary: General rules for beings with Divine Might: ordinary Magic Resistance and Penetration rules apply, they are not omnipotent, they cannot have True Faith, and they are never bothered by The Gift.
quotes: Creatures with Divine Might use the normal rules for determining Magic Resistance, Penetration, and whether their powers can be dispelled.
Creatures with Divine Might cannot have True Faith.
Creatures with Divine Might are never bothered by The Gift.

entries.title: Divine Beings
entries.summary: Defines a divine being as any creature with Divine Might and describes where such beings live and how they interact with humans.

entries.title: Nephilim
entries.summary: Describes the Nephilim, half-angelic giants, including their longevity, immunity to disease and need to eat prodigiously.

entries.title: What Are Angels?
entries.summary: Defines angels as the spiritual inhabitants of Heaven with Divine Might, their membership of a single Choir, and where each Choir tends to be found.

entries.title: Angelic Choirs
entries.summary: Lists the three Hierarchies and nine Choirs of angels, from most to least exalted.

entries.title: Angelic Traits (overview)
entries.summary: Introduces the shared traits all angels have and the extra traits each Hierarchy grants, and how Seferiel from the core book fits.

entries.title: Angelic Traits
entries.summary: The baseline statistics every angel shares: minimum Divine Might, a fixed Personality Trait, the ability to be a conduit for a miracle and obedience to divine law.
quotes: All angels possess the Personality Trait "Love of God" +5.

entries.title: Angelic Characteristics
entries.summary: How to set an angel's Characteristics: non-physical ones derive from Divine Might, physical ones from a point-buy for its Mantle.
quotes: Angels with 1-10 Divine Might have a +1 in all non-physical Characteristics; angels with 11-20 Divine Might have +2 in all non-physical Characteristics, and so on.

entries.title: Angelic Free Will
entries.summary: Guidance on how angels act freely but always in accord with God's will, and notes that they can be wounded or destroyed.

entries.title: Angelic Senses
entries.summary: Angels perceive directly rather than through senses, so their perception cannot be targeted by spells.

entries.title: Angelic Movement
entries.summary: Angels move instantaneously, though in a Mantle they usually move naturally.

entries.title: Angelic Language
entries.summary: Angels communicate by illumination, which has a Penetration of zero, so they often speak human languages to magi.
quotes: This speech has a Penetration of zero (modified by any Penetration Ability the angel may have)

entries.title: Angelic True Names
entries.summary: True Names of angels act as arcane connections and aid Penetration for anyone who learns them.
quotes: True Names act as indefinite Arcane Connections, and grant a +5 multiplier bonus to a caster's Penetration multiplier.

entries.title: Angels and Magic
entries.summary: How Hermetic magic can affect angels in Mantle or in spiritual form, their immunities, and how they can be destroyed.
quotes: angels can be destroyed permanently by reducing their Divine Might to a negative value.

entries.title: Angels, Auras, and Regiones
entries.summary: What angels automatically know about auras, how they enter regiones, and the Second Sight rating they use to find non-Divine regiones.
quotes: All angels are considered to have a Second Sight Ability score equal to their Divine Might ÷ 5 for the purposes of finding non-Divine regiones.

entries.title: Seraphim (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Seraphim.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 35
with the level of the effect determined by the number of Might Points spent multiplied by 10

entries.title: Cherubim (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Cherubim.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 25

entries.title: Thrones (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Thrones.
quotes: The Holy Influence Total of a Throne using this power is equal to his Divine Might ÷ 2

entries.title: Dominations (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Dominations.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 10

entries.title: Authorities (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Authorities, including how Might reflects an Authority's office.
quotes: An Authority responsible for a flower may have Divine Might 5, while an Authority responsible for a thunder storm or a mountain has a Might of 15 or 20.

entries.title: Potentates (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Potentates.
quotes: The cost of the power is equal to the cost of the diabolical power it is opposing.

entries.title: Principalities (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Principalities, including the Might cost scaled to the size of the area protected.
quotes: A family costs 5 Might points, a hamlet or village costs 10, a town or city costs 15, a duchy costs 20, a kingdom or nation costs 30, and an empire, such as Byzantium or the Islamic Caliphate, costs 40 points.

entries.title: Archangels (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by all Archangels.
quotes: Divine Might: No less than 50
doing +40 damage to all non-Divine beings (doubled against creatures with Infernal Might), and stripping non-Divine beings of 10 points of Might

entries.title: Angels (Choir traits)
entries.summary: Minimum Divine Might, Personality Traits and Powers shared by the lowest Choir of angels.
quotes: the angel may modify by 3 (plus or minus) any Personality Trait roll that could result in the target acting virtuously or piously

entries.title: Grigori, the Watchers
entries.summary: Describes the Watchers, a tenth Choir cast to Earth and trapped in their Mantle, and how they can be permanently slain.

entries.title: Portraying Angels
entries.summary: Advice on playing angels as near-perfect but fallible beings, and on how they appear in an Envisioning or in a disguised Mantle.
quotes: Angels can make mistakes, over- or under-estimate someone, and be outwitted or fooled.

gated.title: Demons
gated.intro: Demons and their powers, and the corrupted.

entries.title: Demons and Magic
entries.summary: How Hermetic magic interacts with demons: deceptions and Infernal Might are invisible to truth-revealing spells, Second Sight is harder against them, they can be warded and attacked with Vim, and summoning them is forbidden by the Oath of Hermes.
quotes: Hermetic magic cannot pierce any deception produced by a demon
this Ease Factor is increased by the magnitude of their Might.
a demon that is reduced to an Infernal Might of zero is destroyed, leaving behind no corpse (and thus no vis)

entries.title: Corrupt Beasts
entries.summary: How animals become corrupt (demonic influence, birth, Infernal auras or diabolists) and how to build one: start from a mundane beast, apply the compulsory Corrupted Beast Flaw and balance it with Virtues and Flaws from a restricted list.
quotes: To create the game statistics of a Corrupt Beast, start with the statistics of a mundane beast, and apply the Corrupted Beast Flaw.
The corpse of a corrupted beast typically contains one pawn of vis for each five points of Might it possessed.

entries.title: Infernal Creatures: Demon Basics
entries.summary: Introduces demons and devils as one group, notes that some corrupted physical beings with Infernal Might are not true demons, and states that demons can shed their physical forms at will and are not bothered by The Gift.
quotes: All demons can put off their physical forms and revert to being pure spirits at will.
Demons are never noticeably bothered by The Gift.

entries.title: Demonic Powers (Coagulation, Obsession, Envisioning, Possession)
entries.summary: The powers common to demons: Coagulation to form a body, Obsession to impose a sinful Personality Trait on a mortal (with a worked example), Envisioning for dreams and waking visions, and Possession, which uses a separate Possession Might Pool.
quotes: Manifesting a physical form takes a round for every point of Infernal Might possessed by the demon
the victim's player must make a simple roll and add the Obsession Trait; this must be lower than a simple roll + any other suitable Personality Trait to successfully resist the impulses
the demon may expend any number of points from its Might Pool to create a Possession Might Pool

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal p.75

entries.title: Demonic Weaknesses
entries.summary: Every demon is vulnerable to expressions of God's power and has one extra weakness chosen from a list (abhorrent material, compulsiveness, ordering, protected group, running water, vulnerability). Learning a particular demon's weakness takes a roll.
quotes: must make an Intelligence + Infernal Lore roll against an Ease Factor of 9 + (Might /5)
Subtract 3 from the Ease Factor if the demon is a member of a family

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.41

entries.title: Demons and Free Will
entries.summary: Explains that demons always follow their evil impulses and have no virtues, and that Confidence represents a demon's ability to act rationally against its passions; not all demons have it.
quotes: Demons have no virtues at all, which includes such virtues as patience, courage, and self-control.
Not all demons have Confidence, so some demons are incapable of acting against the dictates of their passions.

related.text: Realms of Power: The Infernal, Chapter 4

entries.title: Religious Limitations on Demons
entries.summary: Religious restrictions on demons: they lose their physical form and cannot spend Might on Holy Saturday, are driven from Jewish households whose sins are atoned between Yom Kippur and Sukkot, and cannot use Infernal Might directly on a Muslim who has recently completed the hajj.
quotes: In Christian lands, all demons are forced to abandon their physical form at dawn on Holy Saturday

entries.title: Demons, Auras and Regiones
entries.summary: How quickly Infernal creatures regain Might: at a constant daily rate normally, faster in an Infernal aura, and not at all in a Divine aura.
quotes: NUMBER OF HOURS TO RESTORE ALL MIGHT: 24 - (2 x Infernal Aura)
MIGHT POINTS RESTORED PER HOUR: Infernal Might / Number of hours
A demon cannot regenerate any Might in a Divine aura.

versions.title: Demons, Auras, and Regiones
versions.summary: Governs how fast a demon regains Might Points normally, faster in Infernal auras, and not at all in a Divine aura.
quotes: Number of hours to restore all Might in Infernal aura: 24 – (2 x Infernal Aura)
A demon cannot regenerate any Might at all in a Divine aura.

entries.title: Virtues and Flaws for Corrupted Beasts
entries.summary: The restricted list of Virtues and Flaws a corrupted beast may take.
quotes: Virtues: Greater Immunity, Greater Infernal Power, Ferocity, Lesser Immunity, Lesser Infernal Power

entries.title: Corrupted Beast (Flaw)
entries.summary: The compulsory Flaw that gives an animal an Infernal Might, a sinful Personality Trait, a repellent appearance and the Tainted with Evil Flaw, while leaving it unbothered by The Gift.
quotes: The creature has been corrupted by Infernal power, and has acquired an Infernal Might of 5.
Corrupted Beasts do not react negatively to The Gift.

entries.title: Greater Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts)
entries.requires: Virtue: Greater Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts only)
entries.summary: How to design a corrupted beast's Greater Infernal Power as a spell-like effect, with its Might cost, initiative bonus and level cap.
quotes: The level of effect cannot exceed the Corrupted Beast's (Infernal Might + 10).
A Greater Power typically costs its magnitude in Might points to activate, and has an Init bonus equal to Qik + magnitude.

versions.title: Greater Infernal Power (corrupted beasts)
versions.summary: Rules for giving a corrupted beast a Power that must penetrate, designed with the Maleficia rules, including level cap, Might cost and Initiative.
quotes: with a level of effect that cannot exceed the corrupted beast's (Infernal Might + 10)
has an Initiative bonus equal to Quickness + magnitude

entries.title: Lesser Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts)
entries.requires: Virtue: Lesser Infernal Power (Corrupted Beasts only)
entries.summary: How to design a corrupted beast's Lesser Infernal Power, which is cheap to use and cannot need a Penetration total (otherwise it counts as a Greater Power).
quotes: The level of effect cannot exceed the Corrupted Beast's Infernal Might.
A Minor power typically costs 0-2 Might points to activate, and has an Init bonus equal to magnitude.

versions.title: Lesser Infernal Power (corrupted beasts)
versions.summary: Rules for giving a corrupted beast a constant or cheap Power that needs no Penetration Total, including level cap, Might cost and Initiative.
quotes: The level of effect cannot exceed the corrupted beast's Infernal Might.
adds 2 to the Infernal Might of the corrupted beast

entries.title: True Names
entries.summary: True Names are the only Arcane Connection to a spirit that has no body; characters buy each with experience in Infernal Lore, and a known True Name aids penetration and synthemata research.
quotes: a +5 bonus to the Penetration Multiplier when penetrating an Infernal creature's Magic Resistance
Each True Name costs 5 experience points

related.text: The Mysteries Revised Edition, Chapter 9: Theurgy

entries.title: What are Demons?
entries.summary: Defines what counts as a demon (any creature with an Infernal Might) and the celestial, terrestrial and Infernal-angel origins, which have no functional differences in play.
quotes: There are no functional differences between any of these groups.

entries.title: The Spiritual Form of a Demon
entries.summary: Rules for a demon in spirit form: unseen and unable to affect matter, immune to non-supernatural wounds and ageing, fast flying, and slain only by loss of Infernal Might.
quotes: spiritual demons may travel ten times faster than a human
can only be slain be effects that deplete its Infernal Might

entries.title: The Physical Form of a Demon
entries.summary: Rules for a demon in coagulated physical form: it can interact with matter and be hurt or slain, heals and ages only in this form, and leaves a corpse that may hold vis.
quotes: typically a pawn for every magnitude of Infernal Might

entries.title: Updating the Bestiary
entries.summary: Guidance for converting the demons in the core rulebook bestiary to the new rules by assigning each an order, the order's general traits and the Powers all demons share.

entries.title: Demonic Might Tables (Order and Rank)
entries.summary: Tables giving the Infernal Might range and relative frequency of ranks for each of the nine demonic orders, plus the extra Infernal Might and equivalent Reputation each rank grants.
quotes: | Master | +5 | 3 |
| Prince | +20 | 9 |

entries.title: Common Demonic Traits
entries.summary: Traits all demons share: Infernal Might, a defining sin as a Personality Trait, and an inability to display virtuous Personality Traits of their own free will.
quotes: A demon automatically fails personality rolls (ArM5, page 18) if succeeding would make it act in a virtuous manner.

entries.title: Demonic Might: Order and Rank
entries.summary: Explains that a demon's Infernal Might comes from its order plus a bonus for its rank, and that the two sources are indistinguishable in play.

entries.title: Demonic Reputations
entries.summary: Demons may have Infernal Reputations known to other demons and infernalists; the highest of these and the rank's equivalent Reputation gives the demon's Hierarchy score used when it is summoned.
quotes: The Hierarchy score of a demon is the highest of any Infernal Reputations it has

entries.title: Demonic Characteristics
entries.summary: How to assign Characteristics to a demon: physical Characteristics are bought with points based on Infernal Might, mental ones with a small allotment, with a minimum physical score and no maximum. Includes example Infernal Reputations.
quotes: Demon Physical Characteristics points: Infernal Might
Demon Mental Characteristics points: 0 – 7 (possibly more for powerful demons)

entries.title: Example Infernal Reputations
entries.summary: Table of example Infernal Reputation titles for each band of Reputation score, useful when giving a demon a Reputation.

entries.title: The Infernal Hierarchy
entries.summary: Introduces the nine-order hierarchy of demons used to classify them, with the caveat that storyguides need not be constrained by it.

entries.title: Infernal Ghosts
entries.summary: How to build an Infernal ghost as a demon: its role determines its order, and it lacks the Coagulation Power and physical statistics.
quotes: Infernal ghosts should be designed like any other demon, except that they have no Power of Coagulation

entries.title: False Gods (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for False Gods: Might limit, usual ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Shroud the Stench of the Pit, The Wealth of Nations and His Master's Voice.
quotes: Personality Traits: Proud +6
for every point of Infernal Might possessed by the demon

entries.title: Spirits of Deceit (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Spirits of Deceit: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Change Form, Trust of the Innocent, Forked Tongue of the Serpent and The Serpent's Oracle.
quotes: The Size of the altered form is limited to whatever is natural for the species
An Intelligence roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is allowed to resist the effect.

entries.title: Vessels of Iniquity (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Vessels of Iniquity: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Form of Wickedness (a special Coagulation), Form of Man and Contagious Obsession.
quotes: A Stamina stress roll against an Ease Factor of 6 is needed every hour
For every victim who comes under the sway of the Obsession, the demon loses a point from its Might Pool

entries.title: Avengers of Evil (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Avengers of Evil: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Punish the Sinner Power, whose wound depends on the victim's unatoned sin.
quotes: he suffers a Heavy wound if this Power penetrates his Magic Resistance
a number of points of damage equal to a simple die plus the sum total of all his sinful Personality Traits

entries.title: Demons of God or Infernal Angels?
entries.summary: Clarifies that Avengers of Evil and Accusers claiming to be angels are treated in game terms as demons with Infernal Might.
quotes: both Avengers of Evil and Accusers are demons, because they have Infernal Might rather than Divine Might

entries.title: Deluders (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Deluders: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Delusion and Duplicate the Magi's Technique-based spell effects.
quotes: A minor illusion which affects an Individual amount of material (such as the demon itself) costs one point
It cannot create any effect with a level greater than its Infernal Might, or duplicate Ritual effects.

entries.title: Aerial Powers (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Aerial Powers: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Elemental Control and Recalcitrance, which inflates the demon's effective Might against control attempts.
quotes: at a cost of 1 Might Point per magnitude of effect
treats the demon's Might as if it were one-and-a-half times its actual Might

entries.title: Furies (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Furies: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Waxing Tide of Humors, Beserker Rage and Endurance of the Enraged.
quotes: must make a stress roll against an Ease Factor of 9
The Furies do not suffer from wound penalties, except on Defense totals.

entries.title: Accusers (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Accusers: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and the Powers Betrayal of the Heart and Whispers Behind the Back.
quotes: This Power lasts for a month.

entries.title: Tempters & Evil Spirits (Demonic Order)
entries.summary: Order template for Tempters and Evil Spirits, the largest order: Might limit, ranks, Personality Traits and Flaws, with no Powers specific to the order.
quotes: Personality Traits: Selfish +5

entries.title: A Life Lacking in Virtue (Demon Psychology)
entries.summary: Demons lack all virtue and cannot be played like immoral humans; spending a Confidence Point lets a demon simulate a virtue for the duration of a situation.
quotes: the expenditure of a Confidence Point allows a demon to simulate a virtue in a particular instance

entries.title: Checklist for Roleplaying Demons
entries.summary: Lists behaviours demons cannot perform and those they can manage only by spending a Confidence Point, derived from their lack of the seven virtues.
quotes: Most demons cannot do the following, except with extreme effort (and spending a Confidence Point, which not all demons have):

entries.title: Virtues & Flaws for Corrupted Beasts
entries.summary: Lists the compulsory Flaw, the Virtues and the optional Flaws that a corrupted beast may be built from.
quotes: Optional Flaws: Horrifying Appearance, Demonic Weakness, Lesser Malediction

entries.title: Ferocity (animal Confidence)
entries.summary: Gives an animal a Confidence score that it may only use in situations that trigger its corrupt nature.
quotes: in such circumstances the creature has 3 Confidence Points

entries.title: Golems (Introduction)
entries.summary: Introduces the golem as the pinnacle of kabbalistic achievement: unliving clay brought to life by Divine energies and usually made to protect a community.
quotes: While Kabbalah is used by Jewish practitioners in place of the Invocation Holy Method, the pinnacle of kabbalistic achievement is the creation of the golem

entries.title: Creating Golems
entries.requires: Ability: Kabbalah; studied the Sefer Yetzirah
entries.summary: Creating a golem takes several seasons: shape clay, then accumulate points toward its Might with an Awaken Golem Total, with a Might cap, botch dice and a limit of one golem per protected community.
quotes: AWAKEN GOLEM TOTAL: Intelligence + Kabbalah + Wonders + Ceremony Bonus + Dominion Aura
AWAKEN GOLEM EASE FACTOR: 30
MIGHT CAP: Kabbalah x 5

entries.title: Standard Golem Traits
entries.summary: Starting attributes for a human-form golem played as a Companion: free Characteristics, fixed Virtues and Flaws, starting Abilities and Personality Traits, and a True Name that cannot change.
quotes: All golems have the Unaging and Improved Characteristics Virtues.
Golems do have a True Name, which is determined during their creation.

entries.title: Empowering Golems
entries.summary: A kabbalist spends seasons designing Holy Powers for a golem and accumulates points with an Empower Golem Total; using powers costs Divine Might points.
quotes: EMPOWER GOLEM TOTAL: Intelligence + Kabbalah + Wonders + Ceremony Bonus + Dominion Aura
A golem may have a number of magnitudes of powers equal to its Divine Might Score.

entries.title: Altering a Golem's Powers
entries.requires: Kabbalist who awakened or empowered the golem
entries.summary: A kabbalist can change a golem's powers, gaining a bonus to the Empower Golem Total by removing an existing power; a worked example follows.
quotes: By removing an existing power, the kabbalist gains a bonus equal to that power's level to his Empower Golem Total.

entries.title: Golem Madness
entries.summary: After a tragedy of hubris, an order to break a mitzvah, or removal from its community, the storyguide rolls a stress die on a table that permanently shifts the golem's Personality Traits or drives it mad.
quotes: the storyguide should roll a stress die, comparing the result to the table below.

entries.title: Destroying a Golem
entries.summary: Gives the three ways to destroy a golem, and how a trusting golem can be commanded into torpor by a member of its community.
quotes: There are three ways of destroying a golem.

entries.title: Vampires as Faeries (vitality from blood and fear)
entries.summary: Establishes that Transylvanian vampires are faeries that feed on blood and on the fear their presence causes, gaining vitality whenever peasant rituals repulse them. Every vampire is unique, with its own rites, limitations and vulnerabilities.
quotes: a vampire is a form of faerie that derives vitality both from blood and from the fear its presence engenders
Every time that a vampire is repulsed by the superstitious rituals of a peasant, the vampire's story is enforced, and it gains vitality.

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie p.12 vitality

entries.title: Becoming a Vampire
entries.summary: Lists the folk beliefs about who becomes a vampire and explains that these circumstances merely attract a faerie which takes the vampire role unless the correct propitiatory rites are performed. Correct precautions feed the faerie vitality so that it moves on.
quotes: these rituals in truth feed the faerie vitality, causing it to become sated and to move on

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie p.12 vitality

entries.title: Precautions Against Vampires
entries.summary: Gives a list of folk precautions of which the storyguide chooses some for each vampire; performing all of them prevents that vampire forming.
quotes: choose one to three items from the following list
If more than one is chosen, all precautions must be met.

entries.title: The Vampire Life Cycle
entries.summary: Describes the phases a vampire passes through from invisible zduhacz to shapeless gadja to human-shaped platenik and finally the long-lived kukudhi, which masquerades as a human and fathers dhampirs.
quotes: Immediately after death, a vampire takes an invisible, ghostlike form (the zduhacz) and haunts the family of the deceased.

entries.title: Creating a Vampire Character
entries.summary: States that vampires are storyguide characters, with only a narrow exception for self-aware kukudhi vampires as possible player characters in a high-power saga.
quotes: Vampires are intended as storyguide characters.

entries.title: Vampiric Virtues, Flaws, and Powers
entries.summary: Lists the Virtues and Flaws every vampire must have when built as a faerie character: a physical form, a cognizance level, a social-interaction trait, Feast of the Dead, a Traditional Ward of sunlight, and the Sap the Life Lesser Power.
quotes: All vampires have the Feast of the Dead Virtue that allows them to obtain vitality from human life, and have a Traditional Ward of sunlight which causes them to take damage if exposed to the light of day.
Finally, all vampires have the Sap the Life Lesser Power (see insert).

entries.title: Common Vampire Virtues and Flaws
entries.summary: Short lists of Virtues and Flaws commonly given to vampires when designing them as faerie characters.

entries.title: Powers for Vampires (sidebar)
entries.summary: Sidebar of ready-made faerie powers for vampires, grouped as Lesser Powers, Focus Powers and Personal Powers, each with Might cost, Initiative and Hermetic-style parameters.

entries.title: Lesser Powers and Converting to Greater Powers
entries.summary: Explains that each Lesser Power Virtue buys a set number of power levels and gives the conversion to a Greater Power by adjusting Might cost and Initiative penalty.
quotes: Each Lesser Power Virtue is a Minor Virtue that grants 25 levels of powers.
halve the Might cost and the penalty to Initiative

entries.title: Sap the Life (vampiric disease power)
entries.summary: A touch power that drains a target's vitality, treated as a disease causing a Light Wound and loss of Fatigue levels, with weekly Disease Recovery Rolls against fixed ease factors. Faerie Lore or Medicine can treat it.
quotes: he must beat an Ease Factor of 12 to remain stable, and a 18 to improve
the victim loses two Fatigue levels which cannot be regained until the disease has abated

entries.title: Ghost Touch (Focus Power for moving objects)
entries.summary: A variable-cost power letting a spirit move or hurl loose objects, with weight limits that scale with Might spent, extra damage for thrown items, and the option to fight with objects; physical attacks must penetrate Magic Resistance.
quotes: For 1 Might point, a maximum of 5 lbs. can be moved; every additional Might point doubles this weight limit.
the item inflicts +5 damage per Might point spent

entries.title: Vampire Personal Powers (Flight, Invisibility, Silent Motion, Supernatural Agility)
entries.summary: Personal Powers are Minor Virtues buying a fixed number of effect levels; the sidebar gives Flight, Invisibility, Silent Motion and Supernatural Agility with their limits (for example no combat while flying swiftly and no flight when heavily encumbered).
quotes: Personal Powers are Minor Virtues, and each allows a character to buy 25 levels of effects.

entries.title: Vampire Limitations (Traditional Wards)
entries.summary: Describes how folk rituals repel vampires because they feed the faerie vitality, and gives a list of limitations of which one to three are chosen for each vampire.
quotes: For each vampire, pick one to three of the following limitations; the vampire has to obey these rules:

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie Traditional Ward

entries.title: Ways to Kill a Vampire
entries.summary: Explains that the correct folk rituals sate a vampire for good, after which the faerie reforms elsewhere, whereas a botched killing lets it return within days or weeks. Lists methods of dispatch of which one is picked for each vampire.
quotes: For each vampire, pick a method of dispatch that results in permanent death:

entries.title: Magi as Vampire Slayers (sidebar)
entries.summary: Warns that simply destroying a vampire and taking its vis does not end the threat, because the community's psychic wound attracts a replacement vampire until the proper rites are performed.
quotes: Even if a magus extracts the vis from the corpse (killing it permanently), another vampire is attracted by the community's wound and takes up where the other left off.

entries.title: Infernal Vampires (broukolak)
entries.summary: Explains that not all vampires are faeries: a demon can consume a corpse and take the deceased's form, and cursing oneself at death attracts one. Introduces the broukolak and its effect on the surrounding area.
quotes: Sometimes, a demon consumes a corpse, and takes the form of the deceased.

entries.title: Living Vampires
entries.summary: Introduces living vampires, human witches and sorcerers who prey on locals but are not faeries and need not drink blood. When they die they attract powerful vampiric faeries.
quotes: Living vampires are witches or sorcerers, who prey on the locals much like the dead vampires.

entries.title: The Strigoi and Vjestitza (living vampire witches)
entries.summary: Describes the strigoi viu or vjestitza, a witch whose spirit leaves her body at night to feed on the heart-blood of victims and who belongs to a coven. Suggests building them as Nightwalkers, infernal witches or faerie wizards.
quotes: These characters are Nightwalkers (Hedge Magic Revised Edition, Chapter 6), but they may have other powers.

related.text: Realms of Power: Faerie Ars Fabulosa

entries.title: The Varcolac and Vukodlak (werewolf living vampires)
entries.summary: Describes werewolf-like varcolaci, how they come about, their wolf brotherhoods that hunt vampires and the mischievous ones that are Nightwalkers. Says which Virtue a varcolac character takes and that they die as bestial vampires.
quotes: A varcolac character has either the Shapeshifter Virtue if he was born a werewolf, or the Skinchanger Virtue if he has learned to change shape.

entries.title: Divine Werewolves (shapeshifting kings)
entries.requires: Crowned Slavic, Magyar or Vlach king
entries.summary: Rules for Divinely favored kings: a king crowned by the Roman and Greek Churches gains Magic Resistance, and a Slavic, Magyar or Vlach one also gets the Shapeshifter Virtue with wolf, lion and dragon forms.
quotes: kings crowned by the religious representatives of both the Roman and Greek Church receive a Magic Resistance of 10
he also receives the free Supernatural Major Virtue: Shapeshifter

related.text: Realms of Power: The Divine p.43

entries.title: Preventing Vampires (hunter practice)
entries.summary: Explains that vampire precautions are done either to the corpse (feet, hands, mouth) or to the place of death, that they work only against some vampire types, and that the Church objects to routine mutilation.
quotes: Most remedies only work on some vampires rather than being universal solutions

entries.title: Killing Vampires (hunter procedure)
entries.summary: Step-by-step approach to hunting a vampire: identify its type, find its daytime resting place (Scry helps), confirm it, ban the grave to weaken it, then destroy it in the exact required way. Includes tactics such as hunting on a Saturday.
quotes: Hunting a vampire on a Saturday is a common tactic, taking advantage of the frequent limitation on vampires that prevents them from spending Might points on a Saturday.
neither a white stallion nor a gander will step over a vampire's grave

related.text: Chapter 8 Ways to Kill a Vampire
